productPageReviews.reviewTitle: FYY Electronic Organizer, Large Travel Cable Organizer Bag Pouch Electronic Accessories
productPageReviews.reviewDescription: The FYY Electronic Organizer is a must-have for anyone who deals with a constant rotation of tech gear and needs to keep their essentials from turning into a tangled mess. This double-layered pouch acts as a central hub for all your chargers, adapters, and specialty cords, making it incredibly easy to see exactly what you have at a glance. The waterproof exterior provides a solid layer of protection for your electronics, and the compact design means you can simply grab the entire bag and toss it into your carry-on or work briefcase without a second thought.What makes this organizer stand out is the logical layout of the interior. The elastic loops and mesh pockets are sized perfectly to hold everything from small SD cards to larger power bricks, preventing items from shifting around during transit. It’s a simple, effective solution that streamlines your workflow by ensuring you aren't hunting through the bottom of a backpack for a specific cable. For a professional who travels frequently, the ability to pack up an entire workstation’s worth of accessories in one organized kit is a massive time-saver.To maximize the storage capacity and prevent the bag from bulging, it is best to **coil your cables using the "over-under" technique** before securing them in the elastic loops. This prevents the cords from developing memory kinks and ensures they lay flat, allowing the double zippers to close smoothly without putting stress on the seams. Additionally, keep your heaviest items—like power banks or large wall plugs—in the bottom compartment to keep the bag's center of gravity stable, which prevents the organizer from tipping over when you have it open on a small airplane tray table or a crowded desk.

items.title: Directions
items.text: Touch the words and pictures to hear words, sound effects, and fun facts; slide the language switch for bilingual play; press the light-up star button for learning songs.

description: Join animal friends Turtle, Tiger and Monkey as they explore new vocabulary in the Learning Friends 100 Words Book. Explore the colorful pages and touch each picture to hear the animals say toddler-appropriate words along with exciting facts and sound effects. Immerse your child in bilingual play by sliding the language switch to hear the words, songs and instructions in Spanish. Touch the pictures to hear silly sound effects in Fun Sounds mode or press the light-up star button to hear two learning songs. Discover new vocabulary with cute learning friends! Intended for ages 18+ months. Requires 2 AA batteries. Batteries included for demo purposes only. New batteries recommended for regular use.
features: Meet learning friends Turtle, Tiger and Monkey who will introduce more than 100 age-appropriate words chosen by learning experts
Word categories include: pets, animals, food, mealtime, colors, activities, opposites, outside and more
Touching the words on the pages plays the words, sound effects and fun facts; hear the Learning Friends theme song and My Favorite Word by pressing the light-up star button
Words, songs and instructions can be heard in both English and Spanish for a full bilingual experience

From the manufacturer
Core Learning Skills: 
Early vocabulary

Meet the Learning Friends! Adorable pals Turtle, Tiger and Monkey are excited to introduce new vocabulary to children. Touch the words and pictures on each page to explore words, fun facts, music and sounds. Flip the language switch and hear the words in Spanish, too. 
Features 
Interactive Pages 
Touch the pictures on each page featuring words from 12 learning categories. 
Three Play Modes 
Explore the book through three different play modes. Hear the words read aloud, exciting sound effects associated with each word or fun facts. 
Bilingual Play 
Flip the switch to learn new words including colors, objects and animals in both English and Spanish. 
Light-Up Star 
Press the light-up star button to hear the Learning Friends theme and My Favorite Word songs. 
Hear From Our Learning Expert 
"Vocabulary skills allow children to express themselves clearly and comprehend what they hear and read. Learning Friends 100 Words Book teaches words in familiar categories to highlight word relationships and includes fun fact and Spanish modes to add layers of learning that go beyond a typical first words book." Carolyn James, PhD, LeapFrog Literacy Expert

productPageReviews.reviewTitle: Easy to use, super light beginner's mini droneEasy to use, super light beginner's mini drone
productPageReviews.reviewDescription: Quite a fun little drone. Delivered in a zippered case with foam cutouts, you get the drone, 4 blade protectors, 2 batteries, 2 USB A to C charger cables, a controller, 4 replacement blades (2 of each type), the instruction manual, a separate app manual, and a screwdriver.Everything is mostly charged out of the box as neither the batteries nor controller took long to top off. While those were charging, I downloaded the app and created the (mandatory) user account required to use it, and familiarized myself with how to connect the app to the drone; basically, connect to it's wireless network and that's about it.I didn't have a good sized indoor space to test it out, but it did alright outside though it had to fight against each gust of wind and I had to frequently re-calibrate it as it would tend to acquire a slide after fighting a rough breeze. It's incredibly small and light and really has to fight against the wind and we had a few 15-20 mph gusts today so it was not optimal weather for this drone.The speed, stability and control are all well suited for a beginner; it slides rather than darts, though the rotation is surprisingly zippy. The auto take-off and landing are super useful, I found it interesting that you can still control the X-Y movement while it's descending, but it was useful for avoiding getting blown into a tree.Feature wise, the app is similar to the 10 other drone apps I have on my phone, and has a plethora of features. Aside from the camera (photo & video plus up and down movement), it also has pathing, hand gestures, speed changes (if you're brave enough), and honestly it had enough features that I didn't get through all of them since I spent a lot of time fighting the wind.I did note that the photos and videos were indeed pretty good quality. Resolution on drones is more about file save size and not about actual quality and this drone camera appears to do a bit better. The video is a bit jerky - as you'd expect from a small drone in the wind without a stablizer - but it's clear, no tearing or blurring, just a bit of stuttering when you do a fast turn.

productPageReviews.reviewTitle: AWESOME FOR: 2nd travel work monitor mainly for document work, for laptopAWESOME FOR: 2nd travel work monitor mainly for document work, for laptop
productPageReviews.reviewDescription: It is key to know what you want this for. I'm not a gamer so this review is only from perspective of someone who works on documents all day, logged into an office remotely. So I needed a portable 2nd monitor for when I travel with macbook M1 Air. Must have read 100 reviews and looked at dozens of youtube videos and ultimately concluded for my use case, I did not need 4K, too expensive and unnecessary; and I do not need high refresh rate, but i did want high nits (brightness). Have tested it out only for a short while and so far, subject to any update I will make to this review, here's the good and the one not so terrible "knock":THE GOOD:For my use case, the 60 hertz refresh rate is totally fine. No doubt not ideal for a gamer; if gaming is your need I would look for one that has higher refresh rate of course.The 1080P is wonderfully sharp - seems like it's better resolution than 1080P but probably just because the screen size is 15.6" so pixel density is still good.It came with several seemingly very good quality cables and a simple charger plug. Charger plug is USB A so it's not giving tremendous current but evidently it's fine. It also came with USB A to USB C cable for this charger plug to power the thing. It also came with a very nice USB C to USB C cable that plugs into one of the two (2) USB C ports (one under the other) on the left side and the other end plugs into USB C on Mac and it instantly just recognized the video stream and showed it, mirroring my Mac. Mac then lets you select to use it as an extended display. Both USB C ports on left side are labeled as USB C with a lightning bolt. I suspect this means both support the video stream and power into the device; I randomly picked one for the video connection and one for the power connection and it worked find; I suspect this means it doesn't matter which. I read on-line in specs that these USB C ports were on different sides, and only one supported video; this one is configured a little differently and perhaps just slightly updated since they wrote out their specs. NOTE - the USB A charging plug got very warm and the metal of the USB A plug was HOT when I unplugged it - I'm thinking I'm going to plug it in for power to a USB C charger to USB C port on device and see if that gives it the power it needs without heating up; will see... maybe but don't want to give it too much current and cause a problem; will think on that. UPDATE: have now used little anker usb c 20 watt charger plug with usb c to usb c for power and that worked fine and the metal usb plug at the charger did not get hot.I tested the two speakers on this monitor, having the Mac choose those speakers (all going through the one USB C cable) and the speakers are fine, just not as good as the speakers on the Mac (not really giving base but otherwise clear and sharp with OK volume). But who cares for this use case.It ALSO came with another seemingly very solid, not cheap, cable that has HDMI MINI on one side, and standard HDMI on the other. I have a USB C to HDMI (standard sized) adapter so I will try that out as well but haven't yet. Left side of the device has the HDMI mini female port for this connection. UPDATE: have now tested the HDMI cable - works fine, zero issues.Over my enterprise level (CITRIX) connection there were zero issues with recognition of the second screen so, voila, remote working with 2 monitors (Mac screen and this second screen).The thing has a bit of heft/weight to it but not terrible; maybe a pound and a half in weight. Feels fairly solidly built, not cheap.Right side has a power on switch and a little "rocker" wheel like the old school volume controls on side of transistor radios; when the monitor came on, I turned the rocker wheel up and it increased brightness to highest level. To me that's a nice direct mechanical capability to up the brightness without having to dig into settings. Naturally I put it to highest level of brightness. But, see below on this topic.UPDATE: have now also plugged it into iPad (Air 5th gen w/ usb c) and it also works perfectly both to mirror iPad or do center stage allowing a couple windows open on the extended display. Rather awesome.Finally it comes with a detachable thin case that wraps around it, covering screen when closed; and folded back using magnetic attachment to back of display, it stands at a couple different angles, similar to typical tablet covers that fold around, like on the iPad. Worked just fine.THE ONE SMALLER "KNOCK" AND A NIT:Brightness: OK so one of my hoped for criteria was high NITS; I'm not so young and wanted a bright screen. Mac M1 Air gives 400 nits; my older Mac used to give 500 nits I believe and to older eyes, BRIGHT display is really helpful. In all my reading of reviews nearly ALL of the lower cost 1080P monitors from companies with unfamiliar brand names said they did 250 nits of brightness but this one said 400. I figured, probably not true but on a black Friday sale at $79 I figured, how could I possibly really go wrong? Well, it came, and it seems pretty close to the Mac display on brightness - huge relief. Then looking at the paperwork that comes with it, it is acknowledged as only 250 cd/m2; and yet, to my surprise, it seems plenty bright and acceptable for my needs. I would NOT think it's worth it to spend another $150 for a display that purports to give 4K as those are the ones that seem to promise more nits.OVERALL I say for the price point, for the sharpness, for the ease of set up, for the cables it comes with, for the ease of use, for the seemingly solid feel to it all, and for a buyer looking for a VERY affordable option for a second "travel" display to bring with a laptop - I find it difficult to believe ANYONE could knock this thing or say it is not well worth it and quite good. A real "gem" of a find on Amazon in my view. I will update this review over time if and as I learn more or have more to note or if anything I say above changes.

productPageReviews.reviewTitle: Overall great value, for the stated purpose of being a portable monitor
productPageReviews.reviewDescription: This is a review of two monitors:MNN Portable Monitor 15.6inch FHD 1080P (no model number listed) M156F01 is marked on the boxArzopa Portable Monitor, 15.6'' 1080P model number: “S1 Table”I ordered the Arzopa monitor first, as kind of an impulse buy.  I was going to be traveling and wanted to take my mini Ryzen 9 PC with me, but it had no monitor.  I found the Arzopa monitor had good reviews and the price was right so I ordered.  Then later I discovered it was a MATTE panel.  I’m not sure how I missed that earlier, but I would NOT have ordered it if I knew that it was matte.Matte finishes on monitors are supposed to be easier on eyes as the matte surface supposedly reduces glare.  But in my experience, there is a problem with this feature.  First, any monitor positioned properly should never have a problem with glare.  For example, you don’t position a monitor facing a large window or another source of strong light.  If your monitor is positioned correctly, glare should not be a possible problem to be solved.  Second, the matte finish on most monitors I have seen tends to greatly distort the picture quality.  Imagine you are standing outside at noon, but the area you are in is foggy.  The view you have of your surroundings (through a light fog) is similar to the picture quality of any matte finish monitor.  At least, in my experience.I was sitting in front of my two large (not portable) monitors, thinking about the mistake I made in ordering a matte finish portable monitor.  And I realized…I was so used to using dual monitors that I would really want two monitors for travel, also.I read some reviews of the MNN monitor and someone described it as a GLOSSY panel.  Perfect.  I decided to order the MNN to use as my “primary” travel monitor with the Arzopa to be used as my “second” monitor for a dual monitor setup while traveling.  That led to mistake number 2.  They are both matte finish.  When I realized this, they had both shipped.  And they were delivered very quickly , both arriving on the same day.I decided to give these monitors a try, and I’m glad I did.  While they are both described officially as “matte”, the picture qualify is closer to what I would expect from a true “glossy” surface computer monitor.  And they both have much more than acceptable image quality.So to compare them:FEATURES:Their features are identical other than their physical controls.  For adjusting these monitors, there is a difference between them, and I PREFER one over the other, as far as controls go.Arzopa has multi-function push buttons on the left to adjust settings like brightness/contrast.MNN has push-buttons and a teeny tiny joystick on the right to adjust settings like brightness/contrast.  I think this is an odd design decision for a -portable- monitor.The Arzopa controls are both more intuitive and (I believe) probably more sturdy / more likely to be reliable over time.  We’ll see if the tiny joystick of the MNN survives a few trips bouncing around in my checked bags.DISPLAY QUALITYI was very pleasantly surprised by the image quality of both of these monitors.  I would rate them both a solid 9/10 on image quality.  I’ve seen better, but only with OLED panels.  Between the two if I had to pick a winner for image quality it would be the MNN.  But the difference is so slight.  I think they both deserve a “9”.  While I can tell they are both matte (and I do not like that) the matte finish of these monitors is not as “foggy” as most matte monitors.  It’s not matte enough to detract from the overall image quality, which is great.The factory settings of both monitors had the brightness (black lefel) set too high.  Brightness is what controls how “black” black items will appear.  If the Brightness is set too high, then something which should be color black will appear to be gray or (worse) even light gray.  After I turned down the brightness a bit on both monitors, the black level of both was very satisfying.Speakers:  I would never try to use speakers on a portable monitor, so I can’t comment on this.  I don’t think the Arzopa even has speakers, but it doesn’t matter, as I would not use those.STAND:They have virtually identical magnetically attached pleather stands that can be used to support the monitors in vertical or horizontal orientation.  The magnets on both are pretty weak.  However, it should be adequate for use on a solid desk or table.  You might not be happy on an airplane if you hit turbulence at all.Summary and suggestion for improvement:I would give both of these a 4-star rating on the Amazon scale.  To earn a 5-star rating I would suggest:1)  Replace the magnetic stand with something that attaches to the monitor more firmly.2) Include a USB-C cable with a right-angle connector on one end.  For dual monitor use, these both have cables sticking out the left side.  If you want to set them side by side, you need to keep them about 2” apart, because the cables interfere with setting them close together, like you want to.  The most obvious solution would be a right-angle USB-C cable.  I have ordered one.  But it would cost nothing for Arzopa and MNN to include this.3) Make the above changes without increasing the price.  If you could do that,  I would rate these monitors a solid 5/5.  There are better monitors for sale.  But for the stated purpose and price?  These are close to what I would want. Very close.FINAL THOUGHT:  (Which One Should I Buy?)There are many portable monitors available with plenty of options in the same relative price range.  The two I am reviewing here are a couple of the most highly rated.  If you are trying to choose between these two specific monitors, I would recommend you buy the Arzopa.  While the MNN has slightly better image quality, they both have really good image quality.  I think the design of the Arzopa is just a bit more appropriate for the stated purpose of being portable.  If you are leaning toward the MNN however, I would not discourage you from buying it.  If you’ve narrowed down your decision to these two specific monitors, I don’t think you can possibly choose “wrong” if you buy only one of them.  They both exceeded my expectations.

The setup process is guided and intuitive.Fire TV Integration:  This is a major selling point.  Seamlessly controlling the soundbar with your Fire TV remote is incredibly convenient.  No juggling multiple remotes!Improved Sound over TV Speakers:  The soundbar definitely provides a noticeable improvement in clarity and depth compared to most television speakers. Dialogue is clearer, and the overall soundstage is wider.Compact Size:  The soundbar's slim profile fits nicely under most TVs without being intrusive.Affordable Price:  This is a budget-friendly option for those wanting better sound without a huge investment.Bluetooth Connectivity:  The ability to stream music wirelessly from your phone or other Bluetooth devices is a welcome addition.What's Not So Good:Limited Bass:  Being a 2.0 system, the bass response is somewhat lacking.  While it adds some low-end presence, it won't satisfy those looking for deep, rumbling bass for action movies or music.  Consider a subwoofer if bass is a priority.Virtual Surround Sound:  While DTS Virtual:X and Dolby Audio are present, the simulated surround sound effect is subtle.  Don't expect a truly immersive experience.  It provides a slightly wider soundstage, but it's not a replacement for a dedicated surround sound system.Sound Quality Could Be Better:  While better than TV speakers, the overall sound quality is adequate, not exceptional.  The mid-range can sometimes sound a bit muddy.Limited Connectivity:  The soundbar primarily focuses on Fire TV integration.  While it has Bluetooth, it lacks other input options like HDMI ARC, which could limit its versatility.Overall:The Amazon Fire TV Soundbar is a good entry-level soundbar for those primarily focused on improving the audio from their Fire TV and who are on a budget.  The seamless Fire TV integration and improved dialogue clarity are its strongest points.  However, if you're a serious audiophile or crave powerful bass, you'll likely need to spend more for a higher-end system.  This soundbar is best suited for casual viewers who want a simple and affordable upgrade to their TV's built-in speakers.

productPageReviews.reviewDescription: I bought a HUGE Fire TV. Perfect for watching movies. Everyone who visited, loved it. “You have yourself a little theater here, “ said my father. However, I felt as if the standard sound coming out of the television, itself, wasn’t enough. That it wasn’t providing the FULL theater effect.I decided to search for a compatible soundbar but they were all well over $100. As if Amazon’s Alexa knew me, I saw this particular sound bar that I liked. It didn’t look too bulky and the reviews said that it was quite easy to install. In days, this soundbar dropped right under $100, to $99.99. SOLD!I LOVE this Fire Soundbar! I love that it is so PERFECTLY compatible with my Fire TV. So much so that I only have to use one, whichever one, to turn the volume up or down. When I turn the television off, using its own remote, the soundbar turns off by itself. So, I never have to worry about it remaining on when it is not in use.I LOVE that it has three settings, one for dialogue, another for music, and another for movies.I LOVE that it was so easy to install! Just TWO cables. One for the power and one to connect the television to the soundbar. The shape at the ends of the cable are the same and you can’t get confused because there is only ONE hole with that shape at the back of the soundbar and at the back of the television. If you were good, as a child, at putting the square peg into the square hole and the round one into the round hole, you will certainly get this. I decided to connect the cable so that I would never have to deal with bluetooth connectivity issues/slowness. Connectivity just seems more secure and direct with the cable.The sound? What a world of difference! Now the package is complete! You get the full theater effect! My family loves to watch movies with me! I love bass. But for those of you who don’t, you are able to make easy adjustments. I LOVE to listen to the introductory sounds right before the movie begins. It makes me feel—-due to the sound—-like I am sitting at the theater.I also LOVE that if I am in the living room and the television is off, and I just want to listen to some music. I can connect my phone via the bluetooth feature, to my soundbar, and use it as a speaker! How cool is that?I HIGHLY recommend this little soundbar, especially for those who already have a Fire Television!

productPageReviews.reviewTitle: Happy for now but not impressed
productPageReviews.reviewDescription: So, I have a insignia fire tv so you would think an Amazon fire soundbar would work perfectly?It was particularly hard to set up, but the issue was that tv speakers wouldn't switch off so I would have an echoing, double effect of audio. The setting said they were off, but they were not. In fact, I couldn't even switch them off normally. Even with nothing connected, I switch them off and still get sound pushed through.I kept trying to fix it. What I had to do was:1) Settings2) HDMI-CEC control3) Switch One Touch Play off4) Turn off Soundbar5) Set Volume to 06) Turn Soundbar back onThat seem to let the soundbar function independently, get rid of the echoing, and get everything to work as described. The downside, the volume will only go up and down at 2 intervals despite what I set it to internally. And, there is no easy way to switch between the TV and sound bar for audio without screwing up the good result I got after working all day on it.Also, make sure you plug into your first HDMI port/Arc port. I had my gaming console set up and didn't realize my intital issue of no sound was the fact that I needed to swap the ports.Frankly, being an Amazon soundbar with and Amazon TV that specifically has a set up for it. I would say the functionality kind of sucks because it it should just work, like it says it should, by following the instructions without having to search up and down for way to keep both audios from playing. Like, the setting say the internal speakers were off despite being a lie and that setting effected nothing. It made it more difficult them it needed to get it to work somewhat normally.I would prefer to set it so volume interval is 1 but I guess to make this usable I am stuck at 2 everytime. And, I better hope that nothing changes and messes it up again in a update to the TV.The sound itself is a improvement, and there is a marked difference between regular and surround sound. It sort of like watching TV versus going to a theater. It terms of the way it fills the room and hits your ear. I can't say that the movie, music, dialogue settings seem to different to me. The size is okay. It just tall enough to not block my screen. The length is just about the size of my dresser. Depth is about 3.5 inches so as long as you have another room in front or to push back your TV, you will be fine.Overall, it is nice but I am not sure if I am total happy I bought it considering it was almost $90 for what I would categorize as works okay. I feel like for that price, and the fact I specifically bought Amazon for the fact I thought it would better with fire tv, that I am not blown away. Happy for now, but not impressed.

productPageReviews.reviewTitle: I love it! Glad I gave it a chance.
productPageReviews.reviewDescription: You probably don’t care to hear the following experience of mine, but I’m going to share it anyway for those of you who may consider Best Buy instead.I wasn’t planning to shop Black Friday, but I was up past midnight and decided to take a look at Best Buy online. There was a JBL 2.0 Mark II sound bar available for $90.99, which I decided to purchase. I received the confirmation email of my purchase as well as the shipping status. Then the following morning I received another email from Best Buy stating that they had to cancel my order and that I was automatically refunded due to them not having anymore in stock and not knowing when they’d get more. I came to find out they were stocked again at full-price only 2 days later. That was pretty disappointing to say the least after some other questionable recent experiences that left a bad impression. Things happen though and I chalked it up to it just wasn’t meant to be. A few days later I saw this FireTv soundbar advertised to me on CyberMonday at around the same price as the JBL one. I looked into it more and one reviewer swayed me to make the purchase. They said they had the same exact JBL soundbar that I had originally purchased from Best Buy and that this Amazon FireStick one is a lot better. I can’t give a second opinion on the comparison, but I am quite happy with this purchase so far.The moral of the story: sometimes things happen or don’t happen because something better is right around the corner. Cliché, but seems to be true.This soundbar is clean looking and packs a punch. I have it right in front of my TV, which blocks the tv sensor a little bit, but I’m still able to use my Fire-stick remote that I already had. The instructions that come with it are simple, but maybe too simple for the average customer. A search on YouTube will get you set up if you’re confused at all, but once you catch on you’ll see how easy is to use. I had trouble connecting it with the HDMI cable on the side of my TV. I have yet to test if another HDMI cable even works there, but I just switched to one of the HDMI slots in back of my TV and that worked.One of the features I like is how you can change sound modes from dialogue to movie and music by the  press of the same button on the remote. The TV doesn’t need to be on to use the sound bar and you can connect to Bluetooth to play music. This is when I turn up the bass!If you’re looking for an upgrade from your tv’s sound and want to have somewhat of home theater experience in your bedroom/small-medium sized living room, I’d recommend this soundbar. I don’t think you can beat it for the price, unless you’re a serious audiophile. If that’s that case, you wouldn’t even be here. You really can’t expect a whole lot in this price range, but you’ll def get your money’s worth!

productPageReviews.reviewTitle: Absolute Junk dont waist your time.
productPageReviews.reviewDescription: Absolute junk. I wanted to love this device. Plugged it in.. followed easy instructions. And then.. over the past two months it was downhill. If your the type of person that watches just prime.. it might be fine. But if your the type to do games.. switch to youtube and other apps this is not worth it.. every channel.. every app you switch to you have to fix something. Youtube is either mumbled or echoing.. Same with other apps. And guess what? If you shut the speaker off.. the next time you switch to another hdmi to play a dvd or a game.. it comes on blaring again even though you turned it off.. And Game systems? It’s a crap shoot. Sometimes you have audio.. sometimes you dont. And if you try and switch anything.. the screen goes black for five seconds in the middle of a battle. I have tried every single setting there is.. Also.. it comes on blaring sometimes. If your spouse is sleeeping and you decide to switch modes? It YELLS.. optical.. HDMI.. or whatever so loud it wakes everyone in the house up!I have tried HDMI connections.. optical.. and bluetooth all have the same issues.. it either has too much bass or its too tinny… This speaker is utterly useless.. UNLESS.. you simply watch one thing.. you dont switch to other hdmi sources … then it will keep your settings. But who does this?One thing more.. This constantly disconnects your tv speakers.. so if you wish to use those instead (such as on certain apps).. you have to go into settings and switch to tv audio output (tv speakers). And guess what? Usually? It’s grayed out.. and you have to unplug your tv for a few minutes.. disconnect the soundbar entirely and unplug it too.. THEN.. replug your tv in.. start it.. go to settings and see if it’s finally “ungrayed” so you can choose tv speakers.. Ive done this multiple times this morning. How the heck is this convenient?

productPageReviewsFromOtherCountries.reviewDescription: Le tournevis est très quali à l'œil. Le revêtement antidérapant est agréable au toucher et aide bien pour la manœuvre. Les embouts fournis ont l'air de qualité et les tailles les plus courantes sont fournies. Je m'en suis servis pour du démontage de carte mères sur les vis d'entretoises, pour des ventilateurs de boitiers et pour visser/dévisser le radiateur d'un Aio. Tout s'est bien passé sans effort et le magnétisme des embouts s'est avéré suffisant pour retenir les différentes vis comme celles des ventilateurs. Sur le premier niveau de couple s'est déjà suffisant pour visser dévisser sans effort et surtout gagner pas mal de temps. Le moteur ne semble pas du tout forcer pour ce genre d'opérations. Le port de recharge est en usb type-c donc super facile à recharger et pratique même si c'est un standard aujourd'hui c'est positif. Au rang des points "négatifs", histoire de chipoter la boite de rangement est en plastique dur pas terrible mais elle est là, c'est surtout l'absence de verrouillage du couvercle qui est dommage, mais bon rien de dramatique. Le fait que cette visseuse soit droite et non pas avec une poignée n'est pas un problème pour moi, au contraire ça évite d'appuyer comme un bourrin et de foirer des vis et/ou abîmer le moteur de l'appareil. Jusque là, un outil très satisfaisant, quali et en plus avec un design sympa à mon sens. Acheté en promo à 35€ c'est parfait. En bref, du tout bon.

productPageReviews.reviewTitle: Easy Setup, Amazing Quality, Unbelievable Price/Value!
productPageReviews.reviewDescription: If anyone gives this less than 5 stars they are a moron. I bought this on prime days while it was $119.99. It seemed cheap enough that it was worth the risk, and I knew Roku TV was a good buy. I’ve had cheap projectors and you usually have to mirror your phone or connect another device to stream anything and it lags and the speakers suck. I ordered this for movie night to surprise my husband but tested it out first. On a textured wall, set about 12’ away, it took up my whole wall and the picture quality was impressive. It connected just like a Roku TV, with a QR code and a couple clicks and it auto focused to determine the best picture size and square it up. I ordered a second one for a birthday gift and bought a cheap $25 screen that had “front and rear projection” in the description. I thought that meant you could shoot a picture to either side but when it came in the materials were so thin I thought maybe it played through to both sides at the same time. We had it halfway between the porch and pool for the 4th and you could see it on either side! Awesome bonus! The speakers are good for sitting close and a small party but we connected a JBL for this. It connected easier than a cell phone. Pro tip, for anyone who didn’t know this, JBL (and a lot of other major brands) speakers can link together so you can sit them on either side or spread them around. If you download the JBL app you can select the mode where they don’t play the same thing (party mode) or where it plays the left and right speakers  in stereo sound. This was definitely worth the $120, but even at average price history of $160 it’s a solid buy and great for a regular tv even. Easy set up for shooting it across the room, to the ceiling or mounting overhead. I am not paid for this ad but I wish I could get a commission because I could sell this to anyone!

I bought this because I accidentally broke my precious 65” TV and I do not have new smart TV money. So this alternative had to work. Thank goodness it did! I replaced my regular TV with a projector and I do not regret it one bit. You can easily replace your TV with this one because of Roku’s format. I’m familiar with Roku so there was nothing to learn on setup. It’s Roku TV as a projector.It’s also better for your eyes, which is good if you have chronic eye strain. It’s naturally better because you’re not looking at a light box but instead projected light. The clarity was better than expected. If you’re going to use a projector as often as a TV, you will benefit more by investing in a quality projector screen instead of a bedsheet or a TEMU knock off. Regular smart TV’s are expensive and this alleviates that struggle.Speaking of, if you don’t have them already, get some good speakers because the sound quality on this just won’t do. It’s a small device, how much sound quality can you expect it to have? Anyway, get some good speakers to enjoy movie nights and regular viewing. It’s super easy to set up too. You won’t effort from setting it up.Lastly, the compromises: it’s not great during the day in a room with abundant natural light. Projected light will strain under external light in its path. I put my screen by a window curtain that I do not open. It’s helps but eh. Doesn’t stop me most days though. The engine is slightly loud at times but it’s one of those sounds you only notice when you turn it off. Sometimes it runs hot but a TV runs hotter and a lot is being asked of it anyway. I may try putting it on a cooling pad.If you’ve read this, just get the thing lol. For its price, oh yeah. My smart tv is no more but I did not suffer because even after the total cost of a projector, new speakers, a projector stand, and a projector screen, I still spent less than HALF of the cost of a fragile smart tv that will break the moment you accidentally throw your remote at it. It’s a great price and it’s worth it.Very last thing: I got a 100 inch projector screen. Imagine that upgrade from a 65” TV. It’s lovey lol

productPageReviews.reviewDescription: I've been trying this out for 2 months now.I decided I wanted this instead of a traditional television. I was hoping it would be reliable and last and the roku feature would be much easier.Well my instincts were correct and this is a winner!!!It is vibrant, bright, and easy to use. Just plug in and sign into your roku account and you're good to go! It pulled all my apps up from my account in 1 second.The picture will be more vibrant the closer you are to the screen you're projecting onto. I used it on an empty light sand colored wall.I usually have it about 5 foot tall and 8 foot wide and it's fine. I close the blinds to do this otherwise you can make the picture much smaller. The saturation of the picture works and the darker the room the better the picture can be seen. if it's overcast or cloudy I can leave the blinds open, it's only when the sun is coming directly in the window without any clouds that I would have issues.There are picture settings, sound settings etc. just like a Roku TV. This was exactly what I was looking for.It's light weight and it would be easy to take to someone elses house.It keeps your account signed on even when you unplug it.: An added bonus If you like to watch TV before bed you are not getting all that blue light pollution right in your face before bedtime.The only criticism I have is the sound. It's ok but I do have to raise the volume up quite a bit and if you want to watch a movie you may want to invest in some speakers.I feel the built in speakers are not as good as my TV speakers but it's barely noticeable and well worth the price, that's the only reason I took away a star is for the sound. I use it everyday and had no issues.

productPageReviews.reviewDescription: This projector exceeded my expectations. This is the first projector that I have ever owned or used. I want something portable enough for when I have to stay in hotels or at work (as a paramedic in Florida, we are occasionally required to stay at work when there are hurricanes that come through). The image quality is great as well. I am pretty sure that there are more expensive projectors with a sharper image out there, but this one is more than good enough for my needs. I haven’t used the projector with my projector screen yet, just watching on the wall for now I actually really don’t even need to use a screen, wall tv is perfectly fine for me while I stay at my parent’s home. Their guest room is east-facing but I have blackout curtains covering the window. It isn’t super dark in here during the daytime but dark enough to enjoy watching wall tv during the daytime. I do plan on purchasing the Aurzen Zip projector for even greater portability, as well as a higher grade Aurzen projector (I can’t recall the model name at this time). In the meantime, if you are on a budget but still want to get a projector, I recommend this one to anyone researching home / portable projectors.

productPageReviewsFromOtherCountries.reviewTitle: Excellent projector at an affordable price
productPageReviewsFromOtherCountries.reviewDescription: I have had the projector now for a couple of weeks and have found it to be of excellent quality at a super affordable price. I have previously used the Roku platform and therefore found the integrated software to be easy to use and quick to load. I was able to install all of the UK terrestrial channels and streaming services I use within a matter of minutes. I was also able to use Apple AirPlay with no issues. Immediately on using the projector for the first time I was very impressed by the auto focus and keystone correction, which effectively meant that I was able to "point and shoot" the projector at the screen. The only consideration was how far away from the screen I had to place the projector. I found about 2m to be the perfect distance to obtain a sharp picture on my 100" screen. At this distance the colours were very balanced, with only a little blurring at the edges of the screen. Without doubt the best results were obtained when in a very dark room, but the picture can be viewed to an acceptable level when the room has some background/natural light. Due to the fact that it is best used in darkness it would be helpful if the remote buttons were backlit. Sound quality from the onboard speakers is acceptable but I enhanced this by using a separate bluetooth speaker. The sound quality is helped by the fact that the cooling fan is very quiet. I would have no hesitation in recommending this projector to my family and friends.

productPageReviewsFromOtherCountries.reviewDescription: I had previously purchased their Aurzen Eazze D1 Smart Projector, and while the two projectors mostly do the same job, I do prefer this one. For one thing, the buttons on the projector are clearer, they light up and are easier to see. Both can be felt under the finger tips, but they cannot actually be pressed, something I would prefer. However, using the buttons on the projector is not necessary with the remote that comes with it. This is also very nice, easy to use and small, with clear buttons on it. I like it more than the other one. Another difference is the deal with Roku tv, which I think is a big improvement. The layout is better designed, and easier to use. You can download an app on your phone and pick out films or different streaming services, though this is also not necessary - all the basics are already found on the projector. The fan is quiet, and I much prefer the sound effects when typing things out/selecting things on screen. It can project a very clear and large image, and the sound is good, though better when connected to Bluetooth speakers, which is very easy to do. Using the cable input ports works well for me, though this projector does not come with an HDMI cable, unlike the last one. I would say that if you’re not too fussed about the specifics, and want to save money, the cheaper version works very well, however I think this projector is an improvement - mainly through the Roku update which makes it much easier to use, and has a better design. I am very much enjoying using this projector - its amazing. I have to mention that I enjoy buying from this company too, they’re incredibly helpful and attentive with customer support.

productPageReviews.reviewTitle: Shockingly satisfying in every possible way
productPageReviews.reviewDescription: After spending $1000 in headphones/earbuds in the last 3 years (1 Sony $390, 1 Samsung $350, 1 Google $199), and being disappointed with "cost/benefit" on all 3, I decided to give a shot at this absolutely inexpensive option.But before pressing "buy now" and just purchase it, I decided to do very same work I did when buying the other 3 premium devices, and took my time, reading reviews, educating myself about the company and it's commitment with customers/users, and finally, I went deep into the specs of the hardware, software, and the mobile app (this last one definitely a big plus).At this point you might say: "it's a freaking $30 Bluetooth earbud" just buy, use it, and if doesn't deliver it's promises, then just return it and add another "zero" to the original $30 and buy a premium device.Well, not so fast... I was intrigued by how good it all sounded and I want to use this whole experience to test an assumption I've been carrying for a short while, which is that we've been all scammed and abused with the so called premium priced devices, in other words , if you want the goods, you have to pay much higher price for it. So, I looked into this as an opportunity to unmask my theory and for that I had to put the "works" in place.After blending and filtering all the information gathered (the process even included "unclutter suspicious" reviews), the conclusion was obvious: despite all looking very standard, there was a positively intriguing desire to give it a try, and the result couldn't be more satisfying.Design looks average initially, but it actually reflects a distinct personality with a touch of elegance, specially with the colors available (green was my option and I was not disappointed).The hardware is absolutely underestimated for the price tag, meaning, it has the ability to deliver a sound quality that matches my Sony WH1000 (I listen to audio-music/books/podcasts an average of 6 hours a day) with crystal clear sound nuances, including a sharp treble and a solid bass, and yesssss, a battery life that will get you listening music and talking on the phone for a few days just by a one full charge on the charging case.Call quality... isn't this feature one of the most important components that will drive us towards or far away from a device...Yes!!!! So here it is: Shockingly amazing call quality. They built this right, and the balance between the software and the hardware, is in perfect harmony, 4 mics and AI, cleaning all the "distractions" away from phone conversations, and music listening without any disappointment.And here is the "cherry in the cake: THE MOBILE APP. Again, another well built component of the whole experience. Better than my Sony, Google, and yes, heartbreaking, my Samsung (I'm a big fan of Samsung products).Summarizing, it's not Bluetooth 6.0, not 14mm sound shell, but it's absolutely a shocker of a quality device that only cost me $30, and it gives me peace of mind with call and music-sound quality. Noise Canceling absolutely under your control, through an app designed with everything you need to make it "your way", and satisfy your desire to listen music like a music producer ;)Ps: no one paid me to write this review, and despite the fact that I don't ever right a review, here is one I hope it will add value to your decision.

productPageReviews.reviewTitle: Very good sound for small price. Budget bangers!Very good sound for small price. Budget bangers!
productPageReviews.reviewDescription: Anker Soundcore P30i buds.First and foremost I want to be clear that I am rating these buds purely on their own merit.  Without their software, without any Equalizer, just on how they perform straight out of the box.Baseus and Tozo and Jlabs are some of the names when we think of Budget Bass Buds.  And for those who are looking for good, clean bass... I'd compare these with Jlabs.  For bass, right out of the box, playing music with bass in it, they deliver a clear, audible thump, without the actual pounding vibration.  Right now, I'm listening to Cry Little Sister, from the Lost Boys soundtrack, at volume EIGHT.  (That's not even halfway up my volume bar from my phone).And the base tune soundstage is really, really good.  Especially for a bass tuned base.  The vocals, and background vocals are right up front.  Crisp, clear, and don't sound like they are being overwhelmed by anything.  And I can definitely hear every hit from the bass drums, as well as count the cords on the keyboard.Now I'm at 12, and those bass drums are starting to pound.  Other than it's significantly louder, I'm still hearing good clarity of the different ranges.  I can't say this for my Tozo T18 Crystal buds, without tuning.My Baseus BP1 pros would be creeping over the midrange at this volume on the base tune.Ok, now I'm at 18.  A lot louder than I usually listen to.  The highs are much more prominent over the lows.  Which is the opposite of how a lot of bass speakers work.Honestly, this kind of division of the ranges from a single driver speaker is kind of surprising, especially at 20 to 25 dollars.Battery life is good too.  I have a 10 hour day.  2 hours on the bus, 8 hour shift at work.  With the ANC turned on, they need a quick charge at lunch to carry me home.  With ANC turned off, yeah, I can get back in the door before they need to be charged.  Sometimes just barely, if I've had them cranked up.ANC- on the bus they do pretty good.  Cuts down a lot of the engine and sound noise from the bus.  I can still hear people talking next to me, but at about half what it would be without the buds in.At work?  Well it's so noisy at work even full blown ear muffs aren't making it good.Feel- ok this is subjective, because my right ear canal is different from my left.  In my right, I can feel a bit of pressure when I put them in.  But once in, they're quite comfortable, and I can fall asleep with them in, as a side-sleeper.Bluetooth is good.  Stays connected as long as I'm in range, and range is definitely acceptable.  Definitely better than the chap 17 dollar Onn buds I have.  Easy to pair also.My only real complaint is no front panel to show the charge on the batteries.All said the bass isn't as deep on the base soundstage as Tozo delivers, but it's cleaner.  Tozo also offers much better options in their software, as does Baseus, in some ways.I DO like a lot that SoundCore went the route of making the stems wider, instead of longer.  Having long hair, it's less likely to get caught on the stems, and pull them out.Speaking of pulling them out.  I decided to do some headbanging.  My glasses flew off but these buds didn't budge.Overall though I have no regrets at all, buying these very good sounding set of inexpensive buds.
productPageReviews.reviewedIn: Reviewed in the United States on October 25, 2025Reviewed in the United States on October 25, 2025

productPageReviews.reviewDescription: If I could rate this higher, I would. I am absolutely obsessed with these earphones. I am bedbound and wear earphones all day long to listen to books.COMFORT:I have never in my ENTIRE life found earphones that fit my smallish ears (even with changing the rubber sizing and no matter how expensive). After about an hour, all earphones hurt. (Don’t even get me started on the hard earphones. Those are an immediate no because of pain). I was FLABBERGASTED when these fit (didn’t even have to change sizing) and didn’t hurt at all. They’re so comfortable that I forget I’m wearing them completely. Now, this is a great thing and a bad thing because they’ve now taken a swim in a soapy bathtub and in the toilet because I forgot they were even in my ears. I cannot feel them, which is a totally new experience for me with earphones. I also will fall asleep on my side with them in accidentally. I’ll feel them and don’t really recommend that but it’s still not painful.LONGEVITY:They’re obviously water resistant. They beep if they get water in them. Learned that from experience. They work perfectly fine after their little swims. I’ve had them for several months now, using them about 14 hours per day every day, not exaggerating. They’re so lightweight but fit so well that they never fall out. I haven’t tried working out in them but they don’t fall when walking or rolling in my bed. This is shocking because all others ALWAYS fall out from walking or barely turning my head or bending over.QUALITY:Again, SHOCKED. The sound cancellation is surprisingly good. It has 3 different settings and I can easily change through them with the app or tapping and holding the side button. I’ve used these on 6 different plane rides over my Bose noise cancelling over the head headphones. While those do cancel noise better, the soundcore were easier to keep on throughout the whole day and easier to store because they’re tiny. The noise cancellation on the soundcore during the flight was good enough to cancel out a lot of the plane and surrounding noises. There is a very noticeable difference. I also love that there’s a transparency mode. I use that often so I can hear who is coming in and out of the house while I’m home alone.I have accidentally ripped apart the earphones exposing the electronic interior (after accidentally soaking in water). I thought I was a goner but I just pushed it back together and they worked perfectly still. I was amazed. Even if it didn’t work, I would’ve bought more instantly. I love these so much.The text to speech and microphone for calls is not amazing but I don’t use it for that. I like that you can connect it to multiple devices at once so I always have it connected to my iPad and phone. You just have to make sure your phone is silent when using another device at the same time or your phone will take over the sound.APP:The app is awesome. You can locate your earphones if you’ve lost them by making them ping. I only wish you could ping the whole thing while the earphones are in the case. That is literally my ONLY con.I love that you can pick and make your own soundscapes or have them made for you. The music is so relaxing.CONTROL BUTTONS:Barely have to touch. Work great. I use one touch to pause my audiobooks. Two touches to decrease volume. Three to increase volume. Long hold to change noise cancellation level. You don’t have to press hard but they’re also not too sensitive. They don’t react to me pressing my head into a pillow but sometimes react to certain materials (think the fingertips of gloves you can use with phones). However, this is not common.APPEARANCE:I ADORE the light blue. It’s pale and not overpowering. It’s a calming, “coastal” blue. The case is nice and lightweight. Very easy to throw in any bag. They look very pretty in.ADDED BONUS:These are CHEAP. For the quality they should be much more expensive.I HIGHLY recommend these. They’re more comfortable than Air Pods, bose, beats, and tozo (the other earphones I’ve tried in the past).

productPageReviews.reviewDescription: Bought these and figured I’d give them a try after I saw lots of positive reviews at a super affordable price. I was immediately impressed with these. I guess I’ve always bought the cheap ear buds over the years, and even still rock a wired 3.5mm pair of skull candy buds I had for about 12 years, because these blew me away with how much better sounding they were. These have incredible bass and tone and even have the ability to customize an equalizer to your liking in the app! (No you don’t need the app to make these work.) The app even lets you customize the tap controls which is awesome. They work dual and single, if you want to keep one in the case. Battery life seems decent so far, of course that fades on anything over time. The feature that impressed me the most was the auto noise canceling you can do with these. You can customize this control with custom taps too! When noise canceling is off, the built in microphones allow “pass through” noise which is stereo and directional. While the audio quality of this part isn’t great, it allows you to hear and have conversation while the ear buds are in, while also still being able to play music as normal if you want. What’s wild is when you turn the noise canceling on, they shut all the mics off and it’s COMPLETELY quiet. I’ve never had ear buds that are THIS quiet and noise canceling. The first time I used this feature was in the gym while music inside was blaring. When I turned noise canceling on, I looked up and thought someone instantly cut the music off in the gym entirely cause I couldn’t hear any of it. It was like the power in the whole building went out it was so quiet. For the price of these, I’d say you can’t beat them.

productPageReviews.reviewTitle: Perfect for Small Ears and Excellent Sound Quality
productPageReviews.reviewDescription: I’ve had both the Soundcore headphones and these earbuds, and I’ve been really happy with them. The noise canceling works great, and they’re one of the few earbuds I’ve found that are actually comfortable with my small ear canals. productPageReviewsFromOtherCountries.reviewDescription: I was torn between buying the p30i or the p31i, seeing as the prices were similar and the 31 is a newer model. Initially I liked the p30i appearance though, as the stem is not as long, as well as the case being slightly smaller and also featuring a worthwhile phone stand.I decided to buy the p30i as there was a good lightning deal, and I'm very happy with it so far. Although I have not used the p31i, I can say that the sound quality and volume capability of this p30i is amazing. I'm coming from using the Earfun Audio Pro 3, and the sound quality and volume on these are much better.One clarification I wanted to make is that the description indicates there is no multi-point connectivity. Perhaps this was introduced in a later firmware update, but there is definitely a feature called "dual connectivity" which allows you to connect two devices at the same time.The app is also well designed as there are a number of EQ customizations. The battery life is also excellent so far. I put these on for the first time tonight and have been listening to music for a couple of hours and just finished a phone call that lasted close to 90 minutes, and both earbuds still show 100% battery (I didn't use any noise cancellation during this time). The noise cancellation itself works very well, and for the price of these you really can't go wrong.I was tempted to get the p31i as I saw a great lightning deal that only put it a few dollars more, but I think I'll just keep these for now. The noise control and other functions work perfectly fine, and I'm able to crank the volume pretty loud on these and the bass sounds very good. Like I said, the app provides each you customizations allowing you to select from a lot of presets or customize your own sound, and this is extremely useful and helps enhance the sound in many different ways.Another thing that's nice about these is that the touch sensitivity is very accurate, and much better than other earbuds I have used.
Wow it's just so goodDefinitely worth the valueSo easy to control I love how modern it is with the controlsSound clarity absolutely amazing.💯

productPageReviewsFromOtherCountries.reviewTitle: Excelente! Pontos positivos e negativos na descrição do meu comentário.
productPageReviewsFromOtherCountries.reviewDescription: Achei excelente! E com base nos comentários das avaliações que eu vi aqui... Os pontos importantes pra mim foram:1 - veio muito bem embalado, completo (tem 3 tamanhos da borrachinha pra encaixe no ouvido e o fio do carregador) e carregado;2 - não tive problema com conectividade, reconhecimento de bluetooth, ficar perdendo a conexão por estar mais distante, ou no bolso/bolsa;3 - o encaixe do fone na minha orelha ficou MUITO bom! posso me exercitar, comer, fazer qualquer coisa... que ele não cai!;4 - ele veda o som externo muito bem (abri a gaveta de talheres na cozinha, só com ele no ouvido e a música pausada e não ouvi o barulho dela kkkkk mas, de fato... se tiver no volume, eu diria que a partir de 75%, quem tiver perto de você vai ouvir a música que você tá ouvindo, com certeza...;5 - sobre bateria, eu já escutei 1h sem interrupção, depois 2h30min sem interrupção... e ele ainda tá em 70%! maravilhoso!!;6 -  concordando com vários comentários daqui, esse fone realmente é excelente pra tons graves! escutar november rain, ou alguma do dire straits nele... bom demais!7 - se fosse pra "criticar" algum ponto, eu diria que já os agudos não são tão bons... escutei maria callas, por exemplo e realmente não tem aquele som limpo, que você escuta as notas mais altas com muita clareza... não é que não dê pra escutar, mas eu diria que esse realmente não é o forte dele.Entre, olhando os pontos positivos e os negativos (pouquíssimos)... Acredito sim, que é um fone muito bom e que vale muito a pena!Obs.: quando você usa ele em um lugar muito ventilado, às vezes você escuta aquele barulho de corrente de vento... ele não veda 100%... mas não achei que é algo que afeta de fato o que você tá ouvindo no fone.

productPageReviews.reviewDescription: If I would have known how many channels were still available for free, much less how easy it would be to install an antenna, I would’ve done this so so long ago. Ages ago. I barely paid attention to the install instructions, although they were so very easy. No long booklet of 15 different languages, simple steps that were very user-friendly and how to get set up quickly.The antenna itself is smaller than I expected, which I was happy about. I didn’t pay attention to the measurements listed. I thought it needed to be tall for a signal, I thought it was going be some odd looking thing I was going to have in a weird space out in the open. That could potentially look phallic.  😂 When in actuality, it is so small that it blends in with decor that I have around my television and you can’t even see it. I had no issues with having to find a spot for it to be a clear picture. The first place I put it. It worked perfectly with crystal clear reception.  I don’t know if this is because I have windows in my living room, but I was just shocked and so happy about how easy it was to connect. The instructions say to have it as high as possible, so right now it is on a bookshelf, but, again, because it’s so discreet in size you can’t even see it mixed in with my bookshelf decor.These streaming companies that charge $90 a month JUST so you can see local news, I don’t understand how it’s legal according to FCC. Which, by the way, I checked, the FCC doesn’t regulate pricing of any kind for streaming services, nor what they offer. That’s another topic, but how is that legal? I’m currently on limited income and canceled all streaming services that aren’t somehow discounted by other membership, etc.. I also had some of my streaming services on auto draft and didn’t realize how expensive they had become. Ignorance is bliss, actually no it’s not.Even when I get into a better financial situation, I will not pay for those streaming services again. I’m able to watch local news, which means I can watch for the tornado warnings that I will have this afternoon. As opposed to some of the other “free live TV” streaming that shows “local news” for, yes, I counted, 22 other cities that mean nothing to my local safety or community.One time investment of $19, vs minimum of $89 a month. No counting the free coverage of some football games when the cheapest o found for just one sports channel was $20 a month.The only semi trick to setting it up was really based on my TV, and it had nothing to do with this product. Even then it just took 2 to 5 minutes of patience and reading through the e-manual on my Samsung. Hint: you have to find the feature that has your television search for all updated channels, no matter the connectivity. I also thought that I would have to change the source or input on my remote when I wanted to watch local TV from the antenna coverage, no it loaded into my TVs free channel lineup. So no flipping over even from source/input.Wish I would’ve done this years ago, and certainly will keep it no matter when better financial days 🙏🏻 come my way.

productPageReviews.reviewTitle: No Duds.  Solid Quality.  Go-To Brand.No Duds.  Solid Quality.  Go-To Brand.
productPageReviews.reviewDescription: 6 Stars.I have never - ever - had an issue with Amazon Basics batteries.  And the fact there are no duds and they hold their juice for a long time, enables me to buy a 48-pack with the confidence that they'll be good to the last battery.  I keep them in a resealable bag in a garage fridge with all my other batteries.  Maybe they're fresh and far from their expiration because they sell such high volumes and turn over their inventory.  Or maybe they sell so much inventory because the price is right and there are no/few duds.For what it's worth, I've bought batteries from a national brick and mortar electronics chain and if you open the package and get duds, you can't return them.  I bought in order to replenish my wildlife cameras; that's 8 batteries per camera for several cameras once a year.  Not including remote controls, etc.  Why should I have to buy batteries twice?  Why should I have to make a career out of this?  I don't need the stress their friction-point policies impose.Now, I can see how folks would return them for a refund but put old batteries in the open package and thereby get free batteries.  I get it and it ticks me off that they ruin it for the rest of us.  But if you open the package and get duds, you cannot be issued a refund for this very reason.  This happened to me twice, that is on two occasions I bought batteries at this chain and they were duds.The second time I refused to take no for an answer for a refund and escalated it up and down the store's hierarchy until I got to a decision maker who could override the policy.  But by that time, the damage was done.  What ever happened to considering future cash flows from a customer?It wasn't the money; it was the principle that my money wasn't a dud so the product I receive in exchange shouldn't be either.Do you think I've bought batteries there since?  Nope.  Has it given me less reason to walk into their store and buy anything at all?  Yep, 100% actually.  No more meandering walks to see what's in store.  No more impulse buys.I'll keep buying these.  They're so solid.  Problem solved.

productPageReviews.reviewTitle: Unbeatable Bulk Value for Low-to-Mid Drain Devices
productPageReviews.reviewDescription: When managing a high-density equipment load—from patrol vehicle remotes to household sensors—the cost of name-brand power can scale quickly. The Amazon Basics 48-Pack AA Alkaline Batteries is a pragmatic "stockpile" solution that prioritizes sheer quantity and cost-efficiency over extreme high-drain endurance.Consistent Performance Across Daily GearThese 1.5V alkaline cells are engineered for reliable service in everyday electronics. In real-world testing, they perform on par with standard alkaline competitors when used in clocks, TV remotes, and wireless keyboards.Capacity: They typically deliver around 1900mAh at low discharge rates (200mA), which is competitive for their price point.Compatibility: They work seamlessly in game controllers and standard flashlights, providing steady power without the rapid "voltage drop" found in lower-tier generic brands.Emergency Readiness and Shelf LifeThe advertised 10-year shelf life is a critical feature for emergency kits and low-use equipment.Leak-Resistant Design: The construction includes a triple-layer safety valve to help prevent leaks, making them safer for long-term storage inside expensive equipment like digital cameras or portable radios.Bulk Packaging: The frustration-free cardboard box makes it easy to keep the remaining 47 batteries organized on a workshop shelf without them rolling loose in a drawer.The "High-Drain" RealityWhile these are excellent for most tasks, they have limitations in professional-grade high-drain scenarios.Intensive Use: In high-power devices like RC cars or professional camera flashes, they may only last about 80% as long as premium lithium or specialized industrial cells.Environmental Impact: As single-use cells, they lack the long-term sustainability and cost-per-use benefits of NiMH rechargeables for high-rotation items like Xbox controllers.Final VerdictThe Amazon Basics 48-Pack is a definitive "best bang for your buck" utility. It removes the stress of running out of power for standard household and professional accessories. While they might not be the top choice for extreme high-draw gear, their reliability, quantity, and 10-year shelf life make them a fundamental staple for any organized bench or supply closet.

productPageReviews.reviewTitle: The Battery Pack That Says “I Have My Life Together” (I Don’t)
productPageReviews.reviewDescription: I bought the Amazon Basics 48-pack AA “High-Performance” batteries because I wanted to stop living like a raccoon—scavenging half-dead AAs from junk drawers and blaming “the device” like the device is being dramatic. These show up and immediately give you the energy of a person who owns a label maker. I became insufferable for ten minutes.Let’s talk about that phrase: “High-Performance.” The audacity. It’s an AA battery. It’s not training for a triathlon. But I’ll admit it—these things perform. I put them in an Xbox controller and suddenly I’m playing like I’m sponsored. I tossed a couple into a flashlight and it turned on with the confidence of a guy who says “I got it” while carrying a couch up stairs.The real feature here is the 48-pack. Forty-eight is not a number you buy casually. Forty-eight says, “I’ve accepted that my home contains toys that beep, a clock that lies, and at least one device that only dies when guests are over.” It’s also the perfect amount to feel prepared for an emergency you’ll never actually prepare for. I slid the box into a cabinet and immediately felt ready for a blackout, a hurricane, or my kid discovering the sound effects button on a singing plush animal.They claim a 10-year leak-free shelf life, which is basically Amazon telling you, “Go ahead. Forget about these. You’ll find them in 2036 and they’ll still be fine.” That’s a bold promise, but honestly? I believe it, because these come in that Frustration-Free Packaging that opens like a normal human object. No plastic clamshell that requires bolt cutters and a tetanus shot. At 2AM, I tore it open, heard that crisp cardboard rip, and felt something close to peace.Important note: they’re not rechargeable. And I appreciate how blunt that line is—no flirting, no “maybe if you believe.” Just: Single use. Do not try to give these a second chance. Which is fair. These are the batteries you keep for the stuff you need to work now, not the batteries you put on a charger and then forget for three weeks next to your emotional support cables.Bottom line: if you’re constantly feeding batteries to controllers, toys, flashlights, clocks, and whatever mystery device your house has that only takes AA’s out of spite, this pack is the move. If you’re an “I recharge everything” person, you’ll look at these like they’re a fossil.Pros:- 48-pack means you stop playing “which remote is worth saving” at 11PM- Works across the usual AA battery zoo: controllers, toys, flashlights, cameras, clocks, etc.- 10-year shelf life is perfect for emergency kits and procrastinators- Packaging opens without turning your kitchen into a crime scene- Reliable performance (aka: things turn on and stay on, which is all we ask)Cons:- Not rechargeable — these are a one-and-done relationship- “High-Performance” is hilarious marketing for something that lives in a drawer- If you buy 48, you will briefly feel superior to everyone you know (side effect)Best for:People with kids, game controllers, flashlights, emergency kits, or a household that runs on AA-powered chaos.Not for:Rechargeable-only purists who treat disposable batteries like a personal moral failing.Summary:A 48-pack of calm, competent little power cylinders—because your house deserves better than the half-dead AA you found rolling around with a paperclip and a Lego.

features: Echo Dot Kids: Our most popular and cutest smart speaker with Alexa, made for kids (not a toy). A fun screen-free device kids love to use in their own room.
NEW with Alexa+ - Spark endless learning: Watch kids’ curiosity soar as they explore new topics through interactive conversations, discover fun facts, and play games to test their knowledge.
NEW with Alexa+ - Activate their imaginations: Kids co-create one-of-a-kind stories from their wildest ideas as Alexa asks them about characters and themes they want to include.

NEW Sleep Studio – calming songs, sounds and stories from wellness partners Calm, Headspace and Moshi. Use the Amazon Kids Parent Dashboard to select age-appropriate bedtime playlists and set wind-down reminders from Alexa to reduce bedtime battles and encourage healthy bedtime routines.

Age-appropriate listening: Requested songs from Amazon Music, Apple Music, Spotify, or Pandora are filtered for explicit lyrics. Amazon Kids+ provides access to ad-free podcasts from Wondery Kids & Family and ad-free radio stations from iHeart Radio Family.

Thousands of kid-friendly audiobooks: With Amazon Kids+, kids can listen to popular books from Disney, fiction classics from authors like Beverly Cleary, or kid-friendly non-fiction titles and biographies.
Support their emerging independence: Create fun morning alarms and daily routines with Alexa to support new responsibilities, or automatically play calming ambient sounds as bedtime approaches.

Worry-free for parents: Echo Dot Kids is built with multiple layers of privacy controls, including a mic off button. Parents can easily and remotely monitor what kids are listening to and creating with the Amazon Kids Parent Dashboard app. And if it breaks, we’ll replace it for free with our 2-year worry-free guarantee.

productPageReviews.reviewDescription: I got this for my 2-year-old, and the design alone was a huge win. The little owl look is really cute, and I paired it with the stand so it sits on a tree-style bookshelf in his room. It actually blends in like decor, which I love.So far, he hasn’t tried to grab or play with it much because he thinks it “belongs” on the shelf, which is honestly a plus. It feels like a kid-friendly device without being distracting or constantly handled.Where it’s been most useful is during our nighttime routine. We use it to play music and control other Alexa devices, which makes winding down a lot smoother. It’s been reliable for that and easy to use hands-free when my hands are full.I know there are additional kid-focused features available, but I haven’t fully explored those yet, so I can’t speak to parental controls or educational content at this point.This works really well for routines, but if you’re specifically buying it for advanced kid features, you may need to spend some time setting those up and testing them. Really nice if you have your hands full and want to adjust your digital thermostat, set up an alarm, play music.Best for: parents who want a cute, simple smart speaker to support daily routines rather than a fully interactive toy.Keep in mind, you need to purchase the nest separately but they are very cute together even though it blocks the blue light at the bottom that let’s you know the owl is thinking.

productPageReviews.reviewTitle: Boo! I'm not paranoid about who's listeningBoo! I'm not paranoid about who's listening
productPageReviews.reviewDescription: I'm almost 70 and if someone wants to listen in on my world they will be very disappointed.But really; I love this little owl. I live pretty much alone in an upstairs studio apartment and I'm a reader.I wanted the Echo Dot so I can my l just say what I need and someone is cheerfully there to help.It was easy to set up and it was easy to understand after I realized that ask the online info about the hows, what's, an do this was out of date because the new Alexa app radically reconfigured the app. Even when I asked my Echo Dot for help finding Communications it was telling me as if I had the old version. Once I told the Echo Dot I have Alexa V2.268 I learned everything from the Echo Dot itself.I can now waking up to music I like and not the only FM radio station I can get. Now I have my music waking me up and it continues to play more of the same until I say, from my bed, to stop.While I'm getting dressed I ask what's the weather and if there's any news I should know. I have it figure out the calories of the breakfast I'm going to make.We talk about things I'm interested in and it says goodnight and that's nice when you're alone living above a family that reminds me of the joy I had.I ordered the kids owl. It was much less in cost but I wanted the Owl. But getting the kids echo, I got a full year of Amazon kids... not my cup of tea but it says it's a nice perk if you have little kids in your life.The Owl is cute but it has black creepy eyes so I used a paint marker to give him life and sparkle.I did make a child profile just to see how the Echo Dot is with kids and it's wonderful.It asked me to pick two things. I picked a mouse and a log with a hole in it. It created an original audio story that was 3 minutes long and beautiful.I set up notifications about Mom phases, asked for help with the etymology of the word WATER, and asked science questions.It does ask questions back to build your identity of likes and dislikes and that might feel creepy but if you know your child better than the daycare does there's no problem trusting the Echo Dot with your 7 year old up.The music quality it great and it's customized to be just for me and my taste in music.I always buy... today one came on sale with $5 in savings but it was limited time. I saw the spinning orange glow at it's base, meaning I have a message, the Echo Dot out it in my shopping cart but it could have just bought it for me. Yes, you have to be an adult and if you have kids you're going to have to turn that option off in the Alexa app. I deleted the kid profile and unsubscribed from my free year of Amazon kids because that was ridiculously lame.Is Big Brother listening?... Big Brother has been alive since the malls had teams of people asking shoppers if they have time to share their shopping experience. Now the Internet just sells your whole life to the highest bidder... progress and convenience is always listening and watching us.I'm getting another for the living room sso I can talk to my grown kids from my Echo Dot and have use it as an intercom for a guest if they sleep over. My downstairs neighbor has one and offered to give me their info at I could intercom them if ever I needed help.But... the Owl needs a glint in his eyes so as that and have fun at any age.

productPageReviews.reviewTitle: Very easy to set up, easy to use, fun and educational!
productPageReviews.reviewDescription: I absolutely LOVE this Echo Dot!! I got this for my daughter for her 6th birthday and so far we LOVE IT! It was super easy to set up which I thought it would take an hour to do but you just plug it in and download the Amazon kids app and it walks you right through the set up and your ready to go in 10 min or less! It is so cute and this thing made bed time routine magical! You can set an alarm for bedtime and wake up and it will alert her half hour before bedtime to clean up your toys and brush teeth, etc. and my daughter instantly gets up and listens to it when for me it’s usually a struggle and fight lol I was amazed! It made it fun for her and she gets to create bedtime stories with it to listen to before bed and it put her right to sleep! This thing is great she loves playing her favorite songs during the day and making up stories and learning new facts, you can ask it anything educational and it has the answers I definitely recommend this to anyone with children it’s not only fun but educational and teaches healthy routines and responsibility and learning and fun!
