productPageReviews.reviewDescription: This is technically a 4.5 star rating but I didn’t want to be petty and give 4 stars since there’s no 1/2 star option haha.I’m a child free adult that loved the aesthetic of the kids galaxy echo so much that I took advantage of the trade program of my older dot and got a few dollars off just to get this! The speaker itself goes perfectly with my living room decor and blends in wonderfully. Perfect sound and does the job.I had zero problems deactivating the Alexa kids safety feature so that I can play and do what I please listening to music and giving commands.My reason for taking a half star off is the unsightly WHITE cord. Sweet baby Moses man! Lol. It sticks out like a sore thumb and takes away from the sleek look of the dot. Either a black cord should have been included OR if amazon is going to make more cool color themed dots (Adults should be included) the cords should match the speaker.I’m going to look into the echo stage to go wire free but it makes more sense just to up the price of the dot to make it completely wireless with the option for battery or charging. In lieu of buying all of these pointless accessories. There are more basic speakers that have this capability. Echo should follow suit!

productPageReviews.reviewDescription: *Update*Don't be like me and not thoroughly read all the instructions and look at all the pictures. Something kept tickling the back of my brain about the lock that I'd missed something important so I went back and looked at the instructions and locking mechanism...I missed the part where you can make it longer! With some elbow grease and a dish towel (it is slightly greasy and kept slipping from my grip) I was able to turn the latch 90 degrees, pull out, then pull back the 90 degrees to lock the length in place and ta-da! It lined up perfectly. After feeling rather foolish for a minute that I missed that I easily put the front and back plate on and easy peasey the lock works perfectly and was SO easy to install. So don't be a me, if it is too short, make sure you have it extended to the full length before you give up.Original:Bought this a while ago and finally got some time to install. Apparently I did not do my measurements right on the front door because the deadbolt does not fit. The actual deadbolt itself is also smaller than the one I had previously, which just feels less secure.My old dead bold has a slot where I thought I'd be able to make this one work with it. Was able to fully connect everything, was excited...until I realized that it holds the lock (deadbolt knob may be better wording) about a 1/4" to the right of the unlock position. I'm sure there is a way I can fix this, I just got a bit defeated and gave up for the time being so I can go back with fresh eyes and attitude. I'll update it if I'm able to adjust it.For now, I can manually lock and unlock the door with the key, but the electronics don't work (they try) because the knob for the lock is not set to one of the three positions.I got this as a set, so I have one for my backdoor too. Now knowing the measurements, I checked between the two doors and the front door bore hole is about 1/2 inch deeper in than the back door (so I probably measured the back door assuming they would be the same, silly me). So I have a better feeling that the back door will go on smoothly, I just got frustrated and a bit defeated feeling and had to walk away from the project, so it'll be something I try next weekend. (I also have a different style of the same brand I tried next and that one just about ended me, I have steel wrapped doors and it requires three holes to be drilled in to secure it...hence the over-dramatic feelings, that one is the one I really lost it on).

productPageReviews.reviewDescription: Pros:-cost.  for what it is worth, I purchased this lock on sale at $55.  (probably its appropriate price point for the lower tech niche.)  it was so inexpensive compared to Wyze locks and other higher end tech that I bought the $10 extended warranty because some of the reviews of this and other similar locks had maybe 5% rate of 1-star reviews with cheap plastic hardware failures causing those customers frustrating problems.  so far, so good.-function.  it's a no-problem code reading lock.  doesn't allow 1234 or 0000 type basic codes.  no word on battery longevity yet or hardware condition after a frigid midwest winter.  I have this installed on a covered entryway door, so I have my fingers crossed it will hold up.  it reads codes no prob and takes about 1-1.5sec like it says to go from practically instantly recognizing the fingerprint to opening the bolt (see video).  fast enough to be convenient and not have to carry key or enter code.  the manual lock/unlock from inside is straightforward enough and comfortable.-setup.  easy.  i watched an amazon reviewer's 2-min install video before ordering this product.  it's seriously simple, I'd say even for very low-tech people.  if you can wield a screwdriver and have a sense of how doors work, installation should be no problem.  programming it is easy as pie with clear and simple instructions included with redundancy.  took me about 15 minutes at an easy pace from unboxing to final programming.  my kid needed some help to get his fingerprint aligned but got it on the 2nd try and had fun doing it.-appearance.  some of the 'non-brand name' locks on Amazon have somewhat off-putting unrecognizable brand names printed on their face.  I didn't want that.  felt cheap.  this hides brand and has a very appealing look on the bronze plates.  it's OK on the inside.Cons:-lower tech.  obviously, if you're getting this lock for this price, you don't want or need higher tech.  maybe this should be a pro.  but if you want bluetooth, geofencing, wifi, alexa/Siri to run your house, forget it.  you can still give codes and keys out with this... and up to 20 fingerprints.-unknown durability.  if you're seriously worried about security and people busting your lock in, this is a lower grade lock like most entry-level ones.  get something fancier and more expensive if you care about deterring would-be thieves with sledge hammers, crow bars, etc.

Product description
The 80W soldering iron kit is a great premium option for basic soldering needs, soldering jobs, and hobby projects.
Insulated Silicone Sheath: Non-slip, high temperature resistant material, soft and comfortable, and it can effectively relieve fatigue.
Why should you choose Liouhoum 80W Soldering Iron? 
This smart soldering Iron is lightweight and portable. And it has more other features, such as heating up fast, working well, more sturdy, temperature memory, temperature calibration, conversion between Celsius and Fahrenheit, fault alarm indication and Auto sleep Functions. Great fit for basic soldering needs, It is widely used in soldering circuit boards, mobile phones, guitars, jewelry, appliance repair. It is very worth trying for you to choose this soldering iron as a gift for your friends. 
Please note: Do not touch the soldering iron tip with your hands every time the power is turned on for heating. If you touch the tip of the soldering iron with your hand when the power is turned on for heating, the soldering iron will trigger the protective device and stop heating, which is to protect you from burning injuries. After the soldering iron tip is heated, do not touch the tip to avoid high temperature burns and injuries to you. Holding the insulated handle of the soldering iron with one hand is the correct posture. 
Automatic Sleep 
In the power-on state, If the smart soldering iron is placed continuously for 5 minutes, it will auto decrease temperature to extend heating core lifetimes (LCD displays "OFF"). (Holding the handle like normal use ), it will resume heating. 
Rapid Heating Up & Safer 
New upgraded insulation flame retardant design, and it's safe to use. Inner-heated ceramic technology makes the 80w soldering iron heat up very quickly (heat up in 10s). Premium ceramic heating core has a long service life. 
LCD Displays & "+" "-" Keys 
The HD LCD screen can clearly display the temperature. Easy to control temperature. Press "-" / "+" key to decrease or increase the tip temperature. 
5 pcs Soldering Iron TIps 
Types: 900M-T-2.4D, 3C, I, B, K - - (1)Fast heat conduction. (2)Easy to solder. (3)Anti-oxidation soldering head is more sturdy. 
US Plug and Wires 
The wire is thickened by 40%. The interface with an anti-breaking design increases service life. 3 Prong Plug is more convenient and safer. 
Easy to Use 
It is perfect for soldering beginners. Heat-resistant handles can insulate temperature effectively. No need soldering station, just plug and play. 
Wide Application: 
(1) Welding Beginner, (2) Soldering Teaching, (3) Electronic Repair, (4) Basic Household Toolbox. 
Warm Tips: 
(1) Please read soldering iron instructions in detail first. (2) Keep the cleaning sponge wet during use.(3) Turn the unit off or unplug it when not in use. (4) Please take care of yourself while soldering. 
Packaging includes: 
1 * Smart soldering iron, 5 * Soldering tips, 1 * Rosin core solder, 1 * Rosin flux, 1 * Cleaning sponge, 1 * Soldering iron stand 
Your choice without regret.

productPageReviews.reviewTitle: Pencil: good; accessories and instructions: meh.
productPageReviews.reviewDescription: There's a lot to like about this soldering pencil, and a number of things that are a disappointment.First off, I'm using this pencil exclusively to install hot set brass inserts in 3D printed objects.  Temperature is set to 240°. Did not calibrate.THE GOOD:•  Temperature control with readout. Easily visible numbers.•  Simple temperature setting (2 buttons). Remembers last temp setting•  3-prong plug that actually grounds the tip (good for working on static sensitive electronic parts)•  Quick heating and recovery (didn't time warm-up, but seems close to claim of 10 sec.)•  Works very well out of the box for inserting hot set inserts.THE NOT SO GOOD•  Instructions printed on back of the box, which you are likely to toss unless you cut it out. How about a printed sheet, clearly translated?•  Instructions, especially "calibration," are difficult to follow. Calibration info makes up 80% of the operating instructions. You should not have to calibrate the product. Who has a thermometer that goes to 320°C, anyway?•  Haven't tried the included solder. The sponge for tip cleaning is about half the size of a postage stamp and easily lost.•  One video shows a nice plastic case and printed instructions. Product comes with neither.Complaints aside, the pragmatic approach for installing inserts is to try it. If the pencil heats too quickly or two slowly, adjust the temperature setting.  Price-wise, it's OK.

productPageReviews.reviewDescription: I'm giving this an initial 5 stars just for being as inexpensive as it is and actually doing what it's supposed to. Though I do not have the experience or the knowledge to test all the claims made in the advertising. What I do know is that my main goal was just to have an inexpensive iron with some way to control the temperature (even if it isn't 100% accurate).And importantly for me was the auto shutoff feature in which it shuts off after 5 minutes if you're not holding it or moving it and comes back on when you pick it up. That seems like a brilliant feature for the price of this thing. And it works. I wouldn't leave it plugged in unattended just as you likely wouldn't do with anything that heats up. And especially knowing that sometimes things that don't cost a lot don't cost a lot for a reason.The included tips are just about the only thing I will ever use out of the rest of the included accessories. The solder seems OK for maybe a couple of quick cheap and dirty jobs. The flux seems nearly useless. The stand is next to useless but you're not going to get a decent stand with a soldering iron this cheap.I tried it out. It works. It didn't combust. I'll call that a win for now and update my review later down the road.A few things of note....The power cord is predictably a little stiff and the strain relief is not the greatest. So you're really not going to want to try using the included stand. You want it in a real stand. Or else you will likely get burned or burn something around your work area.Not much else I can say. My first soldering iron in the 80s was a cheap one from Radio Shack that probably costed more than this. And I'm pretty sure it only came with one tip. I would not buy this expecting something that could stand up to a lot of hard use. Though maybe it would. But I doubt it. It's doubtful anyone with a legit soldering station would bother with this thing.The handle stays relatively cool and I found no issues there when using it.

productPageReviews.reviewTitle: Perfect for Microsoft Teams and podcasting, incredible battery life!
productPageReviews.reviewDescription: If you spend a lot of time on virtual meetings or listening to long audio formats, the Sony WH-CH520 headphones are a fantastic, budget-friendly choice.I use these primarily for Microsoft Teams meetings and listening to podcasts, and they perform beautifully. The built-in microphone captures crisp, clear vocals without picking up a ton of distracting background noise, which is exactly what you want for work calls. Audio playback is sharp and balanced, making spoken-word audio very easy to focus on.A few standout features:Insane Battery Life: They offer up to 50 hours of battery life on a single charge. You can literally go a couple of weeks of heavy daily use without ever plugging them in.Multipoint Connection: You can pair them to two Bluetooth devices simultaneously. I have them connected to both my laptop and phone, and they seamlessly switch over when a call comes in.Lightweight Comfort: The on-ear design is lightweight and well-padded, so they don't give you that heavy, clamped feeling during long marathon meetings.If you need a reliable workhorse headset for daily productivity, calls, and audio tracking, you really can't beat these for the price. Highly recommended!
productPageReviews.reviewedIn: Reviewed in the United States on July 16, 2026

productPageReviews.reviewDescription: I've been using these every single day for the past four months, and I honestly can't believe how good they are for the price!! The battery life is absolutely INSANE. One full charge lasts me almost an entire month, even with daily use. I keep expecting the battery to die, and it just...doesn't!?!The noise cancellation isn't 100%, but I'd say it's around 70%, which is more than enough for me. It does a great job cutting out background noise so I can focus, and the sound quality is fantastic for $30 price range. Comfortable fit, I use for music, podcasts, and movies which all sound clear and balanced. Easy connectivity too with bluetooth on my TV and Apple products.If you're looking for an affordable headset with that classic over-ear look, amazing battery life, and really solid sound quality, I can't recommend these enough. I'm genuinely blown away by how well they've held up!

productPageReviews.reviewTitle: Inexpensive and pretty good quality, lightweight.
productPageReviews.reviewDescription: I bought these because I needed something that would allow me to enjoy music, pod casts and many other videos without being tied to my desk computer or iPhone. One main reason is I needed something that sounded good but nothing overly priced like my AirPods Pro that only get about 2 hours of listening.  These are rated for up to 50 hours. And the best part was the fact they were inexpensive connect to more than one bluetooth device (my M4 Mac mini and my iPhone 14) in addition I needed something to be able to have a conversation if my phone rings while I am on my Mac. and these have worked so far flawlessly.Set up was a bit more then I expected I figured connect via bluetooth and off I would go but no, I did have to download the app to fine-tune the Headphones which wasn't a big deal. While they are not of the highest quality they are perfect for me and my listening needs.Incoming calls were a breeze and everyone I spoke to so far while wearing them had no issues hearing me.  Now, I am a bit amphrehensive about the battery life because at the whole day yesterday of wearing them the battery monitor on my Mac claim the headphones were still 100%. and if that is true then they are even better than I was expecting battery wise.  I did recharge them over night because I wasn't sure if the Mac was telling me the truth.The voice interaction with my phone calls were very clear and I have no complaints.The fit is really nice if you ask me and they are very light weight, after wearing them almost all day I would forget they were on and have to take em off.They are very comfortable to wear and I noticed just how light they were when I pulled them off and carried them over to where I plugged them in to re-charge.Of course it's only been a couple of days so, if I can edit this review at a later time I will do so, if there is a need to. I mean after only a few days these are brand new so I do need to give them more time.  Surprisingly, my ears have not began to sweat with them being on all day, although. I do have issues with my ears being itchy from time to time but that's not because of the headset. That's just my ears.For the price the quality for me is really good.I may listen to a song or two but, I mainly wanted something to last longer than 2 hours if I watch YouTube or other streaming videos on my computer or iPhone. As well, they release my nice wired set that I used, I got tired of tripping over the wire and my office chair rolling over the cord and getting tangled up.  Plus the added convenience of being able to get up from my desk and walk around my Apartment when I need to while I am listening to something is what I was aiming for.The quality again for me is really good, I am not a sound engineer so I could not tell you where on the spectrum of sound they fit but for the price to me they do the job I expect of them.  All around a good pair of headphones for the price.Battery life may not be up to 50 hours because the battery monitor remained at 100% even though I had them on almost all day.  But, they certainly lasted well past the 2 - 5 hours of wearing them compared to a pair of Apple AirPod Pros.  I still want to kick myself for buying the Apple ones not realizing for the price they didn't last very long on a single charge.I highly recommend.
productPageReviews.reviewedIn: Reviewed in the United States on May 2, 2025

productPageReviews.reviewTitle: Happy with our first pair of headphones!
productPageReviews.reviewDescription: My wife and I both got matching pairs (mine is tan hers is pink), and so far we are loving it. Great sound quality and I can talk on the phone with them as well (which I’m not used to). It’s also her first personal pair of headphones she’s ever had which she was (and still is) excited for. The battery life is great and it’s compact for easy storage. My only reason for not giving them 5 is that the headphones aren’t too comfortable in that they make your ears sore after long periods of having them on (due to not going over your ears but instead on them). Also because of the compact build it’s a bit difficult to rest them around your neck (but very comfortable to just have them on the head behind the ears). I’d say it’s still well worth the price and a great buy despite that (also love the colors).

productPageReviews.reviewDescription: The product arrived well packaged.  There was a delivery delay but it was not horrendous and to be expected given that it was ordered during Parime Days,The headphones arrived almost fully charged,  Set up was relatively easy, but you really do need to use their app to complete the set up process.  The app also allows you to change some settings and select equalizer settings that work for you.The switches have a nice feel to them.  They do have raised areas designed to help you find the correct switch by feel.  There are times however when I find that it is easier to adjust the volume using the phone or I remove the headphone to make a change.  This is a very subjective items so you may not have the same issue.  No stars were deducted for that reason.These are an on ear device.  It was not uncomfortable to me, but it did take some getting used to and here again...Personal preference comes into play.  On a warm and humid day you may experience some sweating where the ear cup rides on your ear.  That may allow for some movement / shifting of the headphone depending on what you are doing.  They may thus not work out well for use doing exercising as an example.The sound quality is great at this price point.  I have Bose ear buds.  The sound from this device is not Bose quality and you should not expect it to be Bose quality.  It is good to very good however.  The equalizer settings allow you to control all five typical equalizer settings PLUS a separate adjustment for th4 bass.Paring was easy and fast.  The connection remains stable most of the time.  There is a selection that allows you to select either top quality sound or a more stable connection.  I chose sound quality an the vast majority of the time the connection was stable with no noise present.  There may be times however, that due to local conditions / interference you may have a little popping or very brief drop out.  I have worn these headphones a LOT since they arrived and while I have experienced that, it was very limited.  Now I also have a lot of electric / electronic devices in use on my property and that will may explain what I experienced.  I did have some interference from some household devices when I wass very close to them.The battery life seems to be very good.  I have worn m for several hours and the voice system still indicates 100% at startup. Unlike my Bose products the battery monitoring system is not linear where it will call out 100%, 90%, 80%b etc...  It may call out 100% until the battery hits 50% (As an example) and then te voice system will drop from stating 100% to 50%.  I do not see that as an issue or negative given the very long stated by the manufacturer battery life, and I have no disagreement with their claims about battery life aty this point in time,So again...Thus far I am very pleased with the fit, quality, and sound quality of these headphones.  Do bed aware that tey are NOT noise cancelling.  There will be some outside noise reduction dur to the ear cups of course.

productPageReviewsFromOtherCountries.reviewTitle: Más de lo que esperaba por el precio
productPageReviewsFromOtherCountries.reviewDescription: Muy cómodos, en mi trabajo participo en muchas reuniones virtuales y hay días en que los traigo puestos tal vez 5 o 6 horas seguidas sin quitármelos y no me molestan, a veces hasta se me olvida que los traigo. Excelente conectividad bluetooth con el celular y laptop, se pueden conectar ambos a la vez. En el gimnasio los he usado corriendo y haciendo todo tipo de ejercicios y son cómodos, ligeros y no se mueven. Los he sudado y la cubierta de las almohadillas no se ha dañado nada. El audio es buenísimo, muy bien nivelado y aunque no tienen cancelación de ruido, con un volumen moderado y por las mismas almohadillas, aisla lo suficientemente bien como para que los ruidos o música del gimnasio, por ejemplo, queden muy en el fondo. Nunca ha sido necesario subir al máximo el volumen. Además con la app puedes ecualizar a tu gusto, también recomiendo, si usas Spotify, ecualizar ahí para tener la mejor experiencia posible. La batería dura muchísimo, en 3 meses de uso usándolos en promedio 3 o 4 horas diarias y solo los he puesto a cargar 3 veces. Cargan muy rápido también. El único detalle que les he encontrado es que con mi SmartTV Hisense, jugando Playstation tiene un delay de medio segundo o 1 segundo, y con Youtube cada 40 segundos o 1 minuto "se brinca" o "se come" como 1 segundo tanto del audio como del video. Pero para mi no ha sido problema porque realmente solo los uso para escuchar música desde mi celular y para tener llamadas de trabajo. En resumen, son cómodos, lucen bien, sobrios y de buena calidad, muy buen audio y excelente rendimiento de batería.

productPageReviews.reviewDescription: If you're hesitating about buying this Asus ROG Strix, don't doubt it—buy it. I’ve been using it for a month now, and it has been excellent since day one. Here is a review coming from my experience:Pros:Performance: The CPU and GPU are incredibly powerful; they handle everything with almost 0 problems.Audio Quality: The Dolby Atmos implementation is excellent, even without external speakers or headphones. It sounds crisp and immersive.Build & Cooling: As expected from the premium ROG line, the chassis quality is top-class, and the cooling system keeps thermals well-managed.Screen: For the $1,299 price point, it’s a great panel. It’s vibrant and clear, though I wish it were slightly brighter.Cons:Windows Hello: It’s a nice feature, but it’s inconsistent. It frequently fails to recognize me, forcing me to use my PIN. It should be more reliable, especially in low light.Network Port (LAN): I’ve noticed the physical port feels a bit loose. Sometimes the cable loses connection, which forces a switch to Wi-Fi, incredibly annoying during gaming. I have to position the cable just right to keep it stable. (I recommend checking if your unit has this issue early on).RAM: 16GB is starting to feel limiting in 2026. For a smooth, future-proof experience, I highly recommend upgrading to 32GB or more.Recommendation:-Use it with the AC on if you want to cool your laptop enough so this one doesn't suffer of thermal throttling and if you can afford a great laptop cooler buy it (I recommend Llano coolers.)-Boot from 0 (if you know how to do it): This is for you to start in 0 and avoid Asus services and extra-softwares that it comes by default. Use G-Helper instead of Armoury Crate btw.Verdict: I have zero regrets. Despite the minor issues with the LAN port and the webcam sensor, this laptop is a beast and offers fantastic value for the money.

Why my power bank provide fewer charges than expect? 
Usually an external battery could supply 60%-70% power to other devices. Approximately 30-40% of the battery capacity is lost in circuit heat and voltage conversions.So a fully charged INIU 10000mAh power bank can offer 6000-7000 mAh to your devices. 
How to calculate the possible number of charges? 
"Industry-standard formula: (Power bank capacity × 65%) ÷ Device battery capacity ≈ Number of Charges. 
eg. (10,000mAh Powerbank × 0.65) ÷ 3279mAh iPhone14 battery ≈ 2.0 charges" 
How long does it take to 100% recharge? 
It depends on the power of the wall charger used: 15W charger - 2.8 hrs, 27W fast charger - 2.0 hrs. 
Note: Please recharge via the USB-C port. 
Does it support pass-through charging? 
Yes, our power bank supports pass-through charging. You can charge both the power bank and connected devices simultaneously. 
Is it allowed on airplanes? 
Yes, our 10000mAh power bank meets the regulations of TSA(Transportation Security Administration) for carring board(≤100wh≈27,027mAh).

items.name: Why my power bank provide fewer charges than expect?
items.text: Usually an external battery could supply 60%-70% power to other devices. Approximately 30-40% of the battery capacity is lost in circuit heat and voltage conversions.So a fully charged INIU 10000mAh power bank can offer 6000-7000 mAh to your devices.

items.name: How to calculate the possible number of charges?
items.text: "Industry-standard formula: (Power bank capacity × 65%) ÷ Device battery capacity ≈ Number of Charges.  eg. (10,000mAh Powerbank × 0.65) ÷ 3279mAh iPhone14 battery ≈ 2.0 charges"

items.name: How long does it take to 100% recharge?
items.text: It depends on the power of the wall charger used: 15W charger - 2.8 hrs, 27W fast charger - 2.0 hrs.  Note: Please recharge via the USB-C port.

items.name: Does it support pass-through charging?
items.text: Yes, our power bank supports pass-through charging. You can charge both the power bank and connected devices simultaneously.

productPageReviews.reviewDescription: This inexpensive pen, despite its lower cost compared to namebrand options like Apple Logitech or other big names, meets all the requirements I had in mind when I bought it. Initially, I intended to use it as a personal item for taking notes and illustrating, but I later gave it to my children, and they found it highly suitable for their tablets.The only downside I’ve noticed is that without a screen protector, you might end up scratching the screen. This is expected since the tip is made of hard plastic, not rubberized material. I recommend getting a screen protector to avoid this issue.However, the fine markings on the pen are virtually invisible to the naked eye, so it’s not a major concern if you choose to use it without a screen protector. The overall cost and weight of the pen are excellent, and I have no complaints about its performance.The pen is well-balanced and comfortable to hold, and its weight is precisely calibrated for accurate screen drawing. If you’re looking for an affordable option compared to namebrand pens, this is the one to consider.

productPageReviewsFromOtherCountries.reviewDescription: Ero un po' scettico all'inizio perché il prezzo è davvero basso rispetto all'originale, ma mi sono dovuto ricredere subito. Ho preso questa Metapen per il mio iPad e devo dire che fa esattamente quello che promette senza spendere una fortuna.Come scrive e come ci si senteLa sensazione è ottima, la penna è leggera e impugnarla è molto naturale. La cosa che mi premeva di più era il "rifiuto del palmo" e devo dire che funziona perfettamente: posso appoggiare la mano sullo schermo mentre scrivo gli appunti e l'iPad non si incasina. Si carica veramente in un attimo, basta attaccarla pochi minuti e hai già ore di autonomia. Per chi come me si dimentica sempre di caricare i dispositivi, questa funzione è una salvezza. La batteria in generale dura parecchio, ci faccio tranquillamente diversi giorni di uso universitario.CompatibilitàL'ho provata su un paio di iPad diversi in famiglia (un Air e un modello base più vecchio) e si è connessa subito senza dover fare procedure strane. È magnetica, quindi si attacca bene al lato del tablet e non si perde in giro per lo zaino.In sintesiSe non siete dei disegnatori professionisti che hanno bisogno di funzioni super avanzate, questa penna è la scelta migliore. productPageReviews.reviewDescription: I'm normally wary of Samsung products because you seem to seldom get what you pay for. But I got this on sale to replace my old Asus Zenbook and am thoroughly impressed with the quality. I went with the Ultra 7 processor with 1 TB SSD and 32 GB RAM.The Good:- It's a sexy, sexy machine - thin, sleek, solid build, and capable of the "one-finger open." It looks and feels very similar to a Macbook- Small size charger and its thin design make it portable when you need it to be- Ultra 7 Processor and 32 GB RAM make it snappy and responsive; great for multi-tasking- Updated integrated GPU is more than adequate for most users, including for games that are not graphically demanding- Thermals are much better than a lot of thin laptops I've tried - didn't get super hot at any point when testing it out- HUGE touchpad and responsive fingerprint scanner.- Gorgeous 3K AMOLED screen (to be expected from Samsung)- Conversion to tablet mode was smooth and hassle-free; pen works great- Speaker sound quality was surprisingly good- Keyboard is very similar (in my opinion) to a Macbook keyboard as far as keystroke depth and "clickiness" and I love the quality of my Macbook keyboardWhat Could Be Better?- Battery life on balanced mode is not terrible, but could be better- For the price, it would be nice to have a dedicated GPU rather than integrated- Wish the webcam was capable of facial recognition- Not a fan of the push to integrate Copilot AI and HATE it when manufacturers put the Copilot key on the keyboard (quick remapping in Power Toys fixes that, though)Conclusion:I'm very happy with my purchase. If you are a casual user, want a 16" laptop for work, school, etc. and not looking for a hardcore gaming machine, then I'd say this would be a good choice IF you can get it on sale at a decent price. Yes, they are clearly trying to compete with the more premium Macbook line, but I can't really fault them for that.

productPageReviews.reviewDescription: I spent a ton of money on this laptop to be able to use for work. Everything I own is a samsung so it only makes sense to buy a samsung laptop, considering that it marries up to my phone, watch, tv, and tablet. I use extreme caution when using this laptop because it is crazy expensive and super thin. I used my laptop one night, I closed the lid and set it on the table and went to bed. When I woke up the next day, the screen was cracked. There is NO signs of visible damage. I contacted Samsung customer support and sent the laptop to them to be repaired. They contacted me and told me my warranty is VOID because there is a crack in the screen. Well that is why the laptop is there, because the screen cracked. Now they want me to pay another several hundred to replace the screen. After doing a small amount of research, it appears to be a common problem with the galaxy book screens cracking from the first generation. I guess i will live with the screen having a crack right in the middle of the screen. I am so disappointed in this laptop and Samsung. I paid almost 2 grand for the screen to crack within 3 months and Samsung wont own up to a known problem.

description: The α7R VI offers extraordinary 66.8 MP resolution, 16-stops dynamic range, incredible image quality, and 30fps blackout-free burst speed, thanks to advanced imaging technology refined by feedback from discerning creators. features: The first in the α7R series to feature a fully-stacked Exmor RS image sensor, the A7R VI delivers enhanced image quality with readout speeds up to 5.6x faster*2. Take your shooting to the next level with 30 fps bursts at full resolution*3, 4K 60p without cropping, expanded dynamic range, and reliable low-light AF.

The BIONZ XR2 engine with an integrated AI processing unit delivers dramatic improvements in image and sound quality, power management, and responsiveness. High-speed processing enables up to 60 AF/AE calculations per second,*4 blackout-free shooting, and 8K video, while the integrated AI processing unit enhances subject recognition and illumination estimation for unprecedented shooting support.

Up to 16 stops of dynamic range*6 at low sensitivities supports HDR processing. Outstanding resolution and high sensitivity capture stunning imagery throughout the ISO 100-32000 range. *7 Noise in night scenes is also reduced.

Shoot bursts at up to 30 fps*3 at full 66.8 MP*1 resolution, with AF/AE tracking and no viewfinder blackout. Up to 60 AF/AE calculations per second*4 effortlessly track even complex subject movement. Plus, with the upgraded BIONZ XR2 processing engine and CFexpress Type A card support, capture up to 215 JPG and 65 Compressed (HQ) RAW images continuously*13.

productPageReviews.reviewTitle: A7RVi does it All for lessA7RVi does it All for less
productPageReviews.reviewDescription: For a mid level user that upgraded from A7iV the RVi is superior in every way.  The larger 67MP files can take more time to handle in Creators app and LR but it’s not a big deal.  The rolling shutter is never noticeable to me but I shoot birds and wildlife.  The EVF and screen flipping every which way r huge upgrades.  The noise in compressed raw is hard to say more or less cause the A7iV is my only comp.  When i go pixel peeping the 67MP gives me more room to zoom in an remain Impressed.I always crop my birdie photos so having more pixels gives me room to Zoom!Write speed isn’t noticeable.  And yeah I’ve held the shutter for a few seconds to see when the msg shows up that it’s writing.  But when would u ever shoot like this?  Birding or any wildlife is short bursts.  Otherwise u have a million raws the side thru.  IMHO.I think about the A1ii for a couple reasons.  Managing smaller files in workflow.  Probably a dopey idea as 50 vs 67 is probably not much size savings.  BUT the one thing that I think is better on the A1 ii is the AF system.  I watch videos that suggests locking in to targets and staying locked on is far better on the A1ii.  However some of this could be easily down to my idiot skills.  lol.  IStill learning this camera and perhaps user factor is an issue.Do ur research.  And if u think faster write speed and btr AF locking is crucial and the extra $2.5K don’t matter to u then get A1ii otherwise go for this 67MP superstar and expect improvements with firmware upgrades.Happy shooting.

productPageReviews.reviewTitle: An Incredible Camera Held Back by Accessibility and a Few Strange IssuesAn Incredible Camera Held Back by Accessibility and a Few Strange Issues
productPageReviews.reviewDescription: I really wanted to give the Sony A7R6 five stars. The image quality, resolution, autofocus technology, EVF clarity, and overall capabilities are incredible. As a photographer coming to Sony from Canon, there is a lot here that I genuinely love.Unfortunately, as a legally blind photographer, the interface is one of my biggest frustrations. The exposure information in the EVF, including shutter speed, aperture, ISO, and other settings, is displayed in fonts that are simply too small and thin for me to read reliably. Even with such a beautiful, high-resolution EVF, I struggle to see some of the most basic information I need while shooting.I would love to see Sony add accessibility options through firmware, including larger and bold fonts, high-contrast display modes, and the ability to change interface colors. For my particular vision impairment, some red/orange indicators are extremely difficult to see, while bright white is significantly easier. A camera this advanced should offer more display customization.I’ve also encountered a strange linear gradient/banding effect in some images while shooting around 1/8000 sec. It has appeared somewhat randomly, so I’m still determining the exact circumstances that trigger it, but it is concerning to see from a camera at this level.There is so much to love about the A7R6, and the files it produces can be absolutely stunning. That’s what makes these frustrations stand out even more. Better accessibility options and resolving the occasional high-shutter-speed banding/gradient issue would dramatically improve the experience for me.For now, it’s a very capable camera that I want to love, but I can’t quite give it more than three stars.

33MP back-illuminated CMOS full-frame sensor 
Copper wiring contributes to higher transmission speeds and faster AD (analogue to digital) conversion. Fast sensor readout enables 10-bit 4:2:2 4K recording up to 60p. The sensor also provides improved color reproducibility, low-noise performance, 15+stop dynamic range and increased AF speed. 
BIONZ XR image processor up to 8x processing speed 
The BIONZ XR engine, also used in the Sony Alpha 1 and Alpha 7S III models, provides up to an 8x increase in processing speed. The engine concentrates real-time processing of AF, image recognition and image quality adjustment to minimize processing latency for greatly increased processing power. 
4K 60p recording and 4:2:2 10-bit recording 
Full pixel readout without binning allows 4K 60p recording in Super 35 mode providing high-resolution smooth footage that can be edited to 2x and 2.5x slow-motion when rendered to 30p or 24p in post-production, and 4K 24p or 30p full pixel readout without binning in full-frame with 7K oversampling. 
Beautiful color expression, with S-Cinetone 
The Alpha 7 IV supports S-Cinetone, based on expertise gained through development of the VENICE CineAlta professional cinema camera line. It delivers natural mid-tones for healthy-looking skin color, plus soft colors and gorgeous highlights. 
Real-time Eye-AF for humans, animals, and birds 
The high speed of the latest image BIONZ XR processing engine provides a significant boost to Real-time Eye AF performance, even when the subject is looking up, down, or sideways. It is also possible to use Touch Tracking to initiate Real-time Tracking of any subject in the frame. 
Fast Hybrid AF with improved speed and tracking 
759 phase-detection AF points and 425 contrast-detection AF points with a wide coverage of roughly 94% of the image area for both stills and movie. This vast collection of data is analyzed in real time by the latest powerful BIONX XR processing engine to achieve the AF system's impressive results.

productPageReviews.reviewTitle: Great Camera From a Youtube Creator
productPageReviews.reviewDescription: I’ve been using the Sony A7 IV for content creation for a few months now, and it’s become the camera I rely on for my YouTube videos and podcasts.The best feature for me is the autofocus. Since I often film myself without anyone behind the camera, I need something I can trust. The eye-tracking autofocus is incredibly accurate and keeps me sharp even when moving around the frame. It eliminates one of the biggest frustrations that comes with recording solo content.The image quality is excellent. The 33MP sensor produces detailed video and photos, and the footage has a professional look without requiring a complicated setup. I shoot mostly in a controlled studio environment, and the camera consistently delivers clean, sharp footage that looks great on YouTube. The color science is also a noticeable improvement compared to older Sony cameras I’ve used.The camera has been extremely reliable. I’ve recorded countless videos with itThe menu system is much better than previous Sony cameras, though there’s still a learning curve because of how many customization options are available. New users may need some time to get everything configured the way they like.If I had one criticism, it’s that the battery can overheat after about an hour. I had to buy a fan attachment, but since I’m in a studio it doesn’t bother me very muchOverall, the Sony A7 IV is an outstanding hybrid camera for creators. It’s one of the few things I’ve purchased that still feels like a great investment.

productPageReviews.reviewTitle: Impressive web PC, first time mac user, massive upgrade over a 4 year old Lenovo Yoga 13
productPageReviews.reviewDescription: The neo is really impressive for $600. It has a nice screen, an incredibly rigid aluminum chassis, loads web pages and videos super fast, boots quick. Impressive Bluetooth and WiFi range and performance (Bluetooth is so much better then my old laptop), good speakers(for a laptop), good battery life, a decent keyboard, excellent trackpad, decent web cam, looks nice, low heat output and no vents to get blocked, compact and light. Highly recommended for anyone shopping for a compact web machine.The only negatives on the hardware are: lack of keyboard backlight, the interior edge of the chassis is sharp, not enough to cut you, but enough to be annoying when typing in some positions, not many ports just a normal USB C and a 2.0 speed USB C (both can be used for charging) and screen does not fold flat, so the laptop cannot be stood up against the wall.I was a bit unsure about the Neo because of it using a cellphone chip, but that was not a problem at all. The Neo is super snappy, as fast as my Workstation/Gaming PC when loading web pages and videos. Also I have not noticed any issues with the amount of RAM, 8GB seems sufficient for running a web browser, just as long as you do not go crazy on tabs in Chrome or if you use Firefox that actually manages tabs properly. As a web browser machine I doubt that this will have any performance issues. I am sure that you would hit limits of the mobile CPU if you do did something serious like video editing, but it is more then enough for more casual use.As someone who had never used a mac before I was a bit apprehensive about trying a different OS, but really it has been fine. I mostly just use my laptop to run a web browser, so I do not interact with the OS that much and MacOS is really pretty nice in many ways. The hardest thing to get used to will be the copy paste shortcuts using command instead of ctrl. Mostly MacOS functions about the same as windows, just better. You can just shut the lid on the Neo and it actually shuts off without hardly using any battery and instantly resumes when you open it again. When you do shut it down boot time is super fast. Mac's update system is pretty unobtrusive and just not stupid like windows update. Mac wants you to sign up to all of their AI and cloud stuff, but you do not have to. I did not even setup the app store. The only apps that I wanted were Firefox and a system wide EQ for my earbuds. I found eqMac on gethub, the free version works pretty well. Anyway don't let the different OS scare you away, MacOS is pretty decent and not really that much different then windows. I got used to it in 2 days of use. Also it should get 7 years of software support.Here is a comparison of the Neo with the 4 year old Lenovo Yoga 13 it is replacing. The Lenovo was $550 when new so a very similar price category from 4 years ago. Not sure if this will be useful to anyone so I am putting this at the end, but I figure that a lot of people will be in the same situation switching from a budget windows machine from a few years ago, Overall the Neo is better in almost every way, except for the screen not being able to fold around like the yoga and the lack of a backlit keyboard.The Neo is much faster, it way outperforms the AMD 4650u in my old lenovo when it comes to loading web pages and videos. My old laptop had started really chugging lately when loading YouTube and twitch videos. Not sure it there is something wrong my old laptop it or if web sites have just gotten that much harder to run.My old lenovo Yoga 13 has an absurd amount of flex in the plastic chassis, when you pick up one corner of the device the other edge sags visibly, the keyboard flexes noticeably when typing, the entire chassis will twist with very little effort. The chassis has also cracked in several places and I have been having to superglue it back together to keep the chassis from literally falling apart. The Neo on the other hand is completely rigid you can lift it anywhere, no flex in the keyboard, you would have to really try to do anything to this thing, it is amazing for a laptop of any price, much less a $600 one. Unless you really do something terrible to it I expect the Neo chassis to last well beond the lifetime of the hardware.The battery life on the neo is great, I would say it is about twice that of the lenovo, even though I just put a new battery in my lenovo 6 months ago.The Bluetooth range on the Neo is at least 2 times better, my earbuds would loose connection to the lenovo if I walked 20 feet away to go to the bathroom. I can walk anywhere in the house and stay connected to the Neo, range of about 40+ feet in the house and about 80+ feet outside. Not only the range is better but also Bluetooth connects faster and just works kind of flawlessly, while in windows I constantly had odd Bluetooth issues. This is with just some basic $30 Anker Bluetooth earbuds.WiFI range and throughput is also much better then my old laptopThe yogo 13 had a good screen, so I do not find the screen of the Neo a huge upgrade, it is noticeably more vibrant and it is higher res, although I found 1980x1080 to be fine at this size. Also the Yoga 13 screen could fold all of the way back and around into any position you want and it was touchscreen, so some improvements and some downsides. Still the color on the Neo screen is very nice.The speakers in the Neo are many times better then the the Lenovo, my old Pixel phone even easily outdid the Lenovo, it had impressively bad speakers.The webcam on the Neo is also a big upgrade over the Lenovo, higher res and just better all around.The Neo has a macbook keyboard, so generally it is a very good laptop keyboard. It is not my favorite type of keyboard, but it works quite well and is fast to type.The trackpad is great, it is so much better then any windows computer trackpad that I have used, it functions a bit different so it takes a bit of getting used to, but it is just so much better then windows trackpads.As the Neo uses a cellphone chip it does not really need any cooling, so there are no vents and the chassis never gets hot or even warm. My old lenovo would get uncomfortably hot when charging and I had to be careful not to block the vents when using it on a bed or blanket, but that is not a problem with the Neo. There are no vents to block.Overall this thing is just impressive for $600 and I just do not see any windows laptop coming close to competing for a thin and light web machine. Sure if you want something that can game or do more intensive work stuff, but I just wanted something to run a web browser and this does that incredibly well while also being a beautifully well made device.

productPageReviews.reviewTitle: It's a budget Mac, I won't quibble over minor issues
productPageReviews.reviewDescription: If I were picking nits, I'd trim a half star for some of the cost-saving choices Apple made with the Neo --- worst among them being the lack of a backlit keyboard (or at least printing the keyboard characters in a highly contrasting color --- like white-on-gray and not dark gray on lighter gray).  Also, having only two USB-C ports in close proximity (rather than on opposite sides) seems a poor design choice and having one of those ports be USB 2 in this day and age seems unnecessarily cheap.  However, as I said, these are minor annoyances and don't detract all that much from the elegance of the machine.What you are getting is the cheapest Mac money has ever been able to buy (cheaper even than most 2020 Macbook Air models on the used market.  You're also getting a laptop that's highly portable, powerful, with great battery life, impressive graphics, Apple Intelligence and that can run iOS and iPadOS apps in addition to those for MacOS.I got the Neo as a (relatively) cheap, take-anywhere traveling companion for a trip to the Amazon and Galapagos Islands. I needed to be able to run my usual software and didn't want to expose my primary laptop to the risks of theft, canoe travel, jungle heat and humidity or wet landings.  I took precautions, yes, but the Neo performed perfectly (as I would expect).For all its capabilities and price, I have no qualms about giving the Neo five stars...but Apple better do something about that keyboard in the next iteration.

productPageReviews.reviewTitle: Impressive  but know the real-world trade-offs before you buy
productPageReviews.reviewDescription: I bought this with my own money — not a review unit, not sponsored — so let me give you the real picture.I was skeptical about the A18 Pro chip going in. It's the same silicon Apple put in the iPhone 16 Pro, and the idea of an iPhone chip powering a Mac felt like a compromise. After a few weeks of daily use though, I have to admit it performs much better than I expected. Browsing, productivity work, running multiple apps at once, light coding — all completely smooth. It even handles 4K video editing decently for casual projects. The machine runs completely silent since there's no fan, which is a huge plus if you work in quiet environments.The 13-inch Liquid Retina display is sharp and vivid — text looks great and colors pop — though at 500 nits it can struggle a bit outdoors in bright sunlight. Not a dealbreaker but worth knowing. The build quality feels premium way above the $599 price point. Solid aluminum chassis, lightweight at 2.7 lbs, and the keyboard has a satisfying feel to it. The 1080p webcam is genuinely one of the best I've used on a laptop — way better than what you get on similarly priced Windows machines.Battery life is solid. I'm getting around 9-10 hours of real-world use (web browsing, productivity apps, some YouTube), which tracks close to Apple's 11-hour web claim. The 16-hour video streaming claim is probably accurate if you're just watching offline video.Honest drawbacks: Only two USB-C ports and nothing else. No HDMI, no SD card slot, no MagSafe. If you need to connect anything, budget for a hub. The base model only supports one external display, and the 20W charger included is slow — expect about 2 hours for a full charge. The keyboard also has no backlighting, which was genuinely surprising at this price. And 8GB of RAM is the only option — you can't upgrade it, so if you're a heavy multitasker or plan to keep this machine 4-5 years, that ceiling may bite you eventually.Bottom line: At $599, this is an exceptional value if you're coming from a Windows laptop or upgrading from an older Mac. The A18 Pro is no slouch, macOS is rock solid, and the build quality punches well above its weight. Just go in knowing the port situation and the RAM limitation, and you'll be happy with it.

productPageReviewsFromOtherCountries.reviewTitle: 「あえて小さくする」という正解。持ち物を本質的に絞り込める、究極のミニマルポーチ「あえて小さくする」という正解。持ち物を本質的に絞り込める、究極のミニマルポーチ
productPageReviewsFromOtherCountries.reviewDescription: サイズ感と収納思想 ：ガジェットポーチはつい大容量を選びがちですが、そうすると中身も増えて重くなってしまいます。この「Mini」サイズは、あえて収納力を制限することで、本当に必要なものだけを厳選させてくれるのが最大の魅力です。自分にとっての「一軍ガジェット」だけで構成された、無駄のないパッキングが自然と出来上がります。ビルドクオリティと安心感 ：Thuleらしい質実剛健な作りで、生地の耐久性やジッパーの滑らかさは文句なしの星5です。非常にコンパクトでありながら、内部のクッション性がしっかりしているため、大切なSDカードや小型デバイスを衝撃から確実に守ってくれる安心感があります。実際の使い勝手 ：内部のゴムバンドやメッシュポケットの配置が絶妙です。私はここにモバイルバッテリーと最小限のケーブル、小型の充電器をいれていますが、ポーチ自体の厚みが抑えられているため、バッグの隙間にスルッと収まります。この「どこにでも入るサイズ感」こそが、持ち出す頻度を高めてくれます。総評 ：「たくさん入れる」ことではなく「スマートに持ち出す」ことに特化した名作です。ポーチを小さくすることで、結果的にバッグ全体の軽量化と整理整頓に繋がりました。持ち物を最小限に最適化したい方に、ぜひ手にとってほしい一品です。

items.title: Directions
items.text: 1. Connect the console to your TV using the provided HDMI cable. 2. Plug in the USB power cable to power on the console. 3. Insert 2 AA batteries into each wireless joystick to make them functional. 4. Enjoy playing the games using the wireless joysticks.

description: Founded in 1972, Atari® changed the way we approached gaming – from the way games were designed to the way they were played. Atari’s iconic games, including Asteroids®, Centipede® and Missile Command® have been played by many millions. Half a century later, Atari® ’s legacy endures. The Gamestation Pro has over 200 games, including Atari® 2600, Atari® 5200, Atari® 7800 and Atari® arcade games
features: Officially licensed Atari titles. Titles include Asteroids, Centipede, Millipede, Breakout, Missile Command, Crystal Castles and many more. Game save options.
Packed with over 200 built-in Atari games + bonus titles. Pac-Man & Galaga not included. Full Game list listed below.
Includes Atari console, games instructions, 2 wireless joysticks, USB power cable, HDMI cable, and user manual. System connects directly to TV.
Includes two 2.4 GHz wireless joysticks, inspired by the original Atari joysticks, include paddles for paddle games like Breakout, Warlords and many more.
User Guide Languages: English, French, Spanish, Italian, Portuguese, German, Dutch, Japanese and Arabic. Dynamic RGB LED lights.
Joysticks require 2 AA batteries each (not included). Ensure console is connected to 5 volt, 2 amp, USB-A port; check picture settings on your TV and turn on or select Game Mode.

productPageReviews.reviewDescription: The first one I got was used, so I didn't even bother trying it. I don't blame this on Amazon, but rather the particular seller. I sent it back and ordered another one, which was new.This is a great system. It was easy to set up and get to playing. The selection of games on it is very good, though it is missing some of my favorites. However, the great thing about this system is that you can also play games it doesn't come with using a micro SD card.The console...It's well built and looks quite nice. The placement of the two USB-C ports on the front for wired controller connection is great, especially in comparison to other Atari retro consoles, and even the original 2600. The controller ports being in the back of those was always a bit unwieldy, while being in the front is just natural. The top is simple, with a Power and Home button, the latter of which is also on each controller. The ring lights are also nice looking, and they're adjustable, from the default, alternating rainbow colors to solid white and solid orange. You adjust the lights with the Menu button on the controllers. The USB-C power port and full size HDMI ports are on the back, and well placed. And the best part... the micro SD card slot, which is on the left side. The console has a bit of weight, which adds to it feeling more solid, though some of that weight comes from a metal plate on the inside that they added to make it feel heavier. Still, its heft is nice.The controllers...For most games they're very good. The joystick part feels quite different from a traditional CX-40 Atari joystick, both in its style and the way it feels, but it's quite nice. Not cheap feeling. They have a light ring around the bottom of the joystick, corresponding with the lights around the Power and Home buttons on the console. They also have a small rotatable knob used for Paddle games, and it's actually quite nice. It turns very smoothly, with just a little resistance. Now I say the controllers are very good for "most" games, as some games require the use of more than just the A button, and the positioning of the B and C buttons can make games that require the use of them, such as the Arcade version of Missile Command, much less enjoyable to play, if not downright unenjoyable. Other than that, the controllers are quite good. The weight is also quite nice when the batteries are installed. On the top, there are Home, Select and Start buttons. On the back is a Menu button, a connectivity light, a USB-C port and a power switch.Some people have found that input latency is a problem when using the controllers. Because it uses the common wireless 2.4GHz protocol, other devices that use 2.4GHz, such as routers, TVs, mice, etc. can interfere with the signal, causing issues. However, these controllers can be used wired, though you have to provide your own USB-C to USB-C cables. This will eliminate all of the wireless related latency. And when using them wired, you don't have to use batteries in them, though without the batteries they'll be considerably lighter in weight.With this said, I notice barely any input latency at all when using them wirelessly. The latency is so little that it's nearly imperceptible. In fact, it's less than with both my 2600+ and Flashback 12, and both of those use wired controllers.Other...Though the unit comes with a USB-A to USB-C power cable, it does not come with a power adapter. You need to provide a 5V adapter of at least 2A.It also comes with an HDMI cable.Summary...All in all this is a great system. It's a lot of fun. The selection of games is quite good and the game play is outstanding, even for the paddle games. There is also new firmware available and there are videos on YouTube that give step by step instructions on how to update it. Mine came with version 1.20, and the new firmware is version 1.30. It contains some bug fixes as well as changing the games layout on the screen, making it easier to sort through them.Two pieces of advice:- If you're using a modern TV, make sure to set the TV to Game mode in the picture settings. Without doing so, the latency can be fairly noticeable, as the TV processes a lot of things for the picture. Game mode disables all of that extra picture processing, making the picture response much more real time.- This is an important one. Look at the seller reviews before you buy this, and make sure to buy it from a good one.

productPageReviews.reviewTitle: Exactly what retro gaming needsExactly what retro gaming needs
productPageReviews.reviewDescription: I received this a little more than 24 hours ago, I am impressed with it so far. It has a lot of 2600 games along with a few 5200, 7800 and Arcade games. It has a lot of games I played as a child. It does have a lot of the popular titles for the 2600, just not space invaders pac man or galaga. This was super easy to set up, plug in the USB and HDMI to the TV, install batteries in the controllers and you are up and playing in 10 minutes. The controller works well and is responsive with little to no lag. Mine was shipped with update 1.30 right out of the box and was brand new. There's plenty of game ROMs on the internet to install along with tutorials on YT. Google is your friend on this one. There's tons of free open source games out there written by amateurs based on past games. I wouldn't ever suggest anyone download official ROMS illegally, it's best to pay for them and get them legitimately. I read a lot of the reviews for this on here, and I can't speak to their experience or expectations but it seems a lot of people don't understand that games can be added easily through use of the SD card slot on the side. There's even custom operating systems out there to add to make every game download to have cover art and description just like it has originally, instead of just a list on the SD card. Most ROMS are kilobites in size so a 32gb SD card will afford you space for over 10,000 games. (Yes you read that right 10,000 games). It won't run any  Xbox PS games but the Xbox one controller is amazing on it, right of the box with default button mapping. PS 4 and 5 controllers work but some of the buttons are not standard use. My kids that grew up on Xbox and Wii can't fathom that this was all we had in the early 80's and 90's to do. I still have my original Atari 2600 and brought it out to compare with this. This is so much better, I think some people have a distorted memory of what the 2600 played like after seeing and playing this. The 2600 was like pushing a lawnmower with square wheels compared to this being a riding lawnmower. You can actually connect a USB C cable to the controller from the console if you have any lag on some games a 10 foot cable is all you really need being any farther away than that doesn't seem right as we had to sit 4 feet away from the TV originally because the cords were so short. Anyone that buys this and is disappointed in it needs to search YT for "Adding games to the Atari Gamestation Pro" before they throw it in the trash or return it. But if you still aren't literate enough after watching YT to get more games then ask a 10 year old they can do it for you.

productPageReviews.reviewDescription: Be prepared to be underwhelmed. The joysticks are an abomination to use. The sticks have very little travel. The B button is positioned quite awkwardly on the top of the stick, and the C button is right where you'd grip the controller. The trackball emulator is alright for what it does, but it's awkwardly positioned on the upper right side of the stick.The emulation is fine, but you can do better with OSS and a PC. Which brings me to the real reason this gets ONE star (a half-star if I could).  NO support for firmware update for Mac OR Linux users. So you must have a Windows machine to update the device.In 2023, it's not difficult to provide Linux support for firmware updates. It doesn't have to be simple, nor does it have to have a GUI, though it takes a TRIVIAL amount of work to make a Linux firmware tool. I have made them myself, and i have used them for other devices like keyboards and portable music players. It's a TRAVESTY that in this day and age, you have to keep a Windows 10 (or later) PC around to update firmware for things like this. It's a trivial job to do and nothing Windows has makes it "better" suited for firmware updates. It's as if My Arcade can't port things to Mac or Linux?Fine, if the programmers at My Arcade are not versed in Windows, hire some. But to avoid Mac too? That's tragic.  This could've been a decent emulation station *IF* it had better support for the millions of enthusiasts who like retro gaming but do NOT own a Windows machine.Sad. You really duffed this one, My Arcade.

productPageReviews.reviewTitle: Fun little retro system with 80's vibes
productPageReviews.reviewDescription: First off, there are quite a few games included but unfortunately many of the best Atari arcade and console games were not amongst this collection.  However, that is where the SD Card comes in.  You can use 2600, 5200, and 7800, and other systems ROM images loaded on to the card.Before you start with the SD Card, ensure you update the firmware from their website.  It includes a lot of enhancements as to the SD Card management.  Most of all it allows you to use a folder structure.  From what I have tested, most of the 2600, 520, and 7800 ROMs all work.  I am not sure about the homebrew games, but I've read they are hit or miss.MAME Roms also work.  However I am not sure what version of MAME emulation is being used so not all of my ROMs are loading.  I'm mostly using older retro ROMS which the system can handle.  I wouldn't try using ROMS from the mid 90's or later.  The system is probably not powerful enough to handle most of those.  I've gotten games like moon patrol, Elevator Action, Dig Dug to work, but other older games like Galaga don't load.  I'm sure it is just the ROM version I have and that the correct one would load.I've also attempted NES, Colecovision, Genesis and Intellivision ROMS.  NES and Genesis work (have to be extracted from the ZIP file) but I have not been able to get Coleco or Intellivision to work.  In fact the directory shows empty when I point to them to try and load the games.The controllers I am not a huge fan of.  Although they are similar in style to the Atari 2600, the button placement (especially the B) seems awkward to me.  I've read people have been able to use other controllers but I have not tried yet.  For basic games the controller is fine however.  I do like how they integrated a paddle onto the controller as well.  Another issue with the controller is that I have had a bit of latency once in a while, but most of the time it is fine.Overall definitely worth buying for a mini-retro console even though there are more powerful out there and it has a few quirks.  Maybe they will continue to update features in firmware to enhance it even more in the future

productPageReviews.reviewTitle: Weak 1st impression... but you can improve itWeak 1st impression... but you can improve it
productPageReviews.reviewDescription: This is my new favorite thing. But the out-of-the-box experience is admittedly weak... As this item arrives, it feels quality and the controllers are nice. But the game selection is not impressive (and my favorite console is the Atari 2600) and the UX/navigation is boring and confusing. There are only 130 actual atari games, and its missing many of the classics (probably due to licensing). The other 70 games are random NES/SNES/arcade filler, most of which are bad... Still there is Asteroids, Tempest, Centipede, Missile Command etc and in console and arcade variations. But the end result feels kind of like one of those cheap flashback systems. The controllers are gorgeous and feel very nice though-- in my opinion much better than the original cx40. But the button layout is awkward. Its not a problem for old one button games, but you'll keep forgetting which button is which on a 16bit title. It also includes all the accessories you need but it only has hdmi output. I would prefer an analog option for older tvs but there are adapters available. And the controllers take AA batteries which is kind of a bummer. So out of the box I would give this only 2 stars...Fortunately you can fix a lot of issues yourself. Start by installing the updated firmware (currently 1.30), which seems more complicated than it should be but there are plenty of tutorials on youtube. That improves the interface and rom loading experience. Then you can add a micro sd card of your own roms (games). It currently plays most any game on atari 2600/5200/7800, NES, SNES, game boy/color/advance, arcade (mame2003) and sega genesis/master system/game gear. This is where it really shines. There is no flashy interface for the games currently, just a text list, but new updates keep coming and certainly this will improve with time and hopefully support for colecovision/intellivision and c64. As it stands this is my new preferred way to play atari games, even over the retron77 and 2600+, but of which I also recommend, especially if you have cartridges too.

productPageReviewsFromOtherCountries.reviewTitle: Fun for the nostalgic, but it helps to be a bit tech-savvy.Fun for the nostalgic, but it helps to be a bit tech-savvy.
productPageReviewsFromOtherCountries.reviewDescription: I am a big fan of old school Atari games.  I already had a 2600+ and a 400 Mini, but the Gamestation caught my interest because it also has over three-dozen Atari arcade games included.  I was a bit leery because the included controllers look rather clunky and awkward.I received mine, fired it up, and immediately played several games, including Asteroids, Sky Raiders, and I, Robot.  I also tried out some 5200, 7800, and 2600 games.  The controllers actually work reasonably well.  I thought I noticed a slight bit of lag, so I picked up a USB-C to USB-C cable to connect the controller directly to the console.The emulation is quite decent, and I am pleased with the GSP.I did spend some time downloading and installing the 1.3 firmware update.  It requires a Windows PC and perhaps a bit of tech savvy.  Once this is installed, there are some improvements, and it's worth doing.I have also side-loaded a number of 2600, 5200, 7800, and arcade games, and most (about 95%) run well.Overall, it is a real treat for Atari fans.

Product description
Can it be wall-mounted? Can it also be placed on a desktop? Is it easy to remove? 
Yes, both mounting options are possible, and it’s easy to install and remove. Our package includes a stand and screws for setup, so you can place it anywhere in your home. 
What is the display size? Does the screen support touch operation and anti-glare? Does it have a built-in camera? 
Our digital calendar features a HD 1920×1080 touchscreen display and supports sleep mode. While it does not have a built-in camera, the screen utilizes blue-light filtering and anti-glare technology to protect your eyes and reduce visual fatigue. 
Can it be used offline/without an internet connection? Does it require a subscription? How do I sync the calendar? 
It must be plugged in and connected to the internet to function. All features are available without any subscription fees. Simply download our App and follow the instructions in the manual to automatically sync with other calendar applications. 
Does it support multi-user access? Can events be created directly on the screen? Does it have a reminder feature? 
Yes, it supports the whole family creating events together, with different colors for distinction. It also allows editing events directly on the e-calendar device, and you can set reminders for specific tasks to be completed before a designated time. 
How can I troubleshoot syncing issues? 
Typically, the initial synchronization takes about 10 minutes—please wait patiently for the data to sync. Alternatively, you can enable the device's auto-update feature, as we regularly update the system to improve synchronization efficiency.

productPageReviews.reviewTitle: A wonderful gift (especially for those who love taking pictures)
productPageReviews.reviewDescription: I got this as a gift for my mom during one Christmas since they're a frequent Facebook user and photo taker. I thought it'd be just an okay decoration, but after about two years of them having it, I have to say that it's been a pretty nifty item to have around their house whenever I come over to visit them!There's enough memory on it to store a fair bit of photos and video clips while displaying them on a pretty decent touch screen monitor. It doesn't have the vibrancy of a super high tech and super expensive screen, BUT for the price, it's more than fine. It does need a separate app to upload your pictures on along with a working Wifi connection, but even without internet, it works like a digital photo frame just fine. I thought this frame would break as others have reported for other digital frame in under a year and would at least need one repair, but after about TWO years, it's working great! Mom's still putting pictures on it and they've had no complaints on it whatsoever.The only complaint I do have would just be the overall build materials of the frame. It's just decorated plastic and does feel kinda meh and cheap sometimes. But it has a plain, black frame so it wont be hard to make it fit into any room or home. It doesn't feel TOO frail either. The frame also does have a settings menu to customize things like the timer for how fast the slideshow should go and to see how much storage is left to use.So if you're looking for a gift for someone who takes a load of pictures, I'd give this a go!

productPageReviews.reviewDescription: I bought this calendar during Prime Deals to help get my kids and husband organized with chores, routines, and our daily schedule. I purchased the black 15-inch version, and I can honestly say it’s exactly as described online.It’s super easy to use and very kid-friendly. You can add tasks, events, routines, recipes, meals, and even photos. If plans change, it’s easy to skip or edit tasks without any hassle. One of my favorite features is the rewards section, where you can give your kids stars ⭐️ for completing their chores and routines. It also has a sleep mode, which is a nice bonus, and you can even set time limits to help everyone stay on track and finish their daily chores.So far, I haven’t experienced any issues, and I definitely think it’s worth the money. It’s made organizing our household much easier, and I would absolutely recommend it to my family and friends.

productPageReviews.reviewDescription: I’m really a paper pencil person, and I have a year wall calendar which I love and still use, but it’s quite cluttered with all our family schedules. The problem is that when I’m out and about scheduling/cancelling appointments I only add it to my phone calendar and forget to add it to the paper calendar.  It’s also not easy to find the appointments again later on my phone. This calendar syncs easily with many different calendar apps. It is very straight forward to set up, use, read, and it lets you know what’s going on that day, the next few days or month. Some say it’s a basic calendar that’s not worth the money but it’s perfect for my family. I don’t have to answer the dreaded question of what do we have to do today. Everyone’s schedules are color coded to match my original calendar app. The only complaint I have is that you can’t add to the calendar console directly because it won’t sync back to my phone calendar app.  That still ok though because I don't want anyone else changing things without my knowledge anyway.  I’m not positive it’s worth it for everyone but it’s definitely worth it for me.Update: 2026 It's been nearly three years since I purchased this product, and I still use it daily.  It only just recently started to have problems with the screen, and I worried that I wouldn't be able to do anything about it, first because I purchased it through amazon, and secondly because it's nearly three years old.  I was still hopeful, so I contacted customer support.  They were quick to respond walked me though trying to fix the product on my own.  I really appreciated their wonderful customer service, so I changed my review from 4 to 5 starts.  I figured it was time for a new calendar anyway, and was thinking about switching to another brand, but the customer service alone is worth staying with this brand.  Skylight is touted as the easiest to setup and use, and I also don't want to have a device with ads or extra busy screens.  You can add or remove information currently showing on the screen, and I want my family to see only what is important.  I didn't mention in my original review that I also easily sync to other calendars, like the kids' sports, school and everything else.  Just so you're aware there's a little bit of a learning curve if you don't already know how to do these things, but I think most people nowadays do.  Since I purchased my original skylight there have also been several improvements to the base model without the subscription.  I don't subscribe to plus and I still highly recommend it.

productPageReviews.reviewTitle: A Great Help for People Suffering Cognitive (Short Term) Impairment
productPageReviews.reviewDescription: The Skylight Calendar was recommended to help anyone with mild cognitive impairment/short term memory issues. We're using it initially too supplement paper wall calendars, daily diaries and piles of individual and confusing paper notes. We are hoping it will replace all of those analog prompts since it can do all of them in a much cleaner format with its integrated events, lists, and tasks all in one easy to see place. We have it hanging on a kitchen wall at eye level. Just have to convince the user that it is much more comprehensive and easier to read than the refrigerator calendar. In our case I've disabled the photo stream screen saver (great way to display all your favorite shots) until the key user is comfortable tapping the screen to view the calendar. Just a touch switches views from month to week to day to event details. We're only two, but this product is great for families as it also can list chores, even with rewards for doing them, recipes, etc. You can even email event info, recipes, tasks, etc. directly to the Skylight. Highly recommended!
